AI.tldr: A single topology-agnostic, touch-based mesh estimator reconstructs full deformable-object shapes from few touches without vision, generalizing across 1D ropes, 2D cloths, and 3D soft bodies. It achieves substantial error reduction vs baselines, and uses deep-ensemble uncertainty to guide where to touch next, with stronger gains under self-occlusion; vision does not require deliberate touch strategies when available.
AI.motivation: Reconstruct accurate full shapes of deformable objects when vision is unavailable or occluded. Touch data are sparse and local, and existing approaches are often topology-specific or rely on continuous vision; a unified, topology-agnostic, touch-only estimator is needed.',
AI.method: A single topology-agnostic estimator leveraging a permutation-invariant cross-attention architecture that operates on 1D/2D/3D deformable objects (rope, cloth, volumetric soft body). It handles touch observations and latent mesh information; uses deep ensemble to quantify uncertainty; demonstrates active-touch policy by selecting next touch based on model uncertainty; compares against non-learned geometric mesh completion, Gaussian-process surface baseline, and a simple global-pool encoder.
AI.result: Reconstruction error is reduced by roughly two-thirds compared with non-learned baselines and Gaussian-process surface baseline. The estimator outperforms a simpler global-pool set encoder, with the gap increasing as more touches are observed. Deep-ensemble uncertainty supports a touch-policy that lowers error further, outperforming random touching and GP-active baselines at sparse budgets. Gains are modest on average but grow with self-occlusion and in the error tail. When vision is available, the need to optimize where to touch diminishes, motivating the vision-free setting studied.
AI.conclusion: A versatile, topology-agnostic, touch-based estimator enables robust full-shape reconstruction of diverse deformable objects without vision; active-touch guided by model uncertainty yields further improvements, particularly under occlusion, validating vision-free tactile sensing as a viable paradigm.

title: EXPLORE: Exploration with Guided Search for Analog Topology Generation using Language Models
summary: Automating analog circuit topology design is essential to reduce the extensive manual effort required to meet increasingly diverse and customized application demands. Recent advances have applied sequence-to-sequence fine-tuning on pretrained language models to directly generate circuit topologies from user specifications in a single pass. However, these one-shot generation methods failed to generate complex circuits due to their exponentially growing search spaces and limited training datasets. In this paper, we present EXPLORE, a search-enhanced framework that integrates simulator-guided Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) with transformer-based decoding to enable test-time scaling for analog topology generation. By leveraging language-model priors and bypassing high-confidence structural tokens, EXPLORE allocates expensive simulator budget primarily toward topology-altering decisions during search. On a 6-component benchmark at a tight tolerance of 0.01, EXPLORE raises the success rate from 12% for one-shot generation and 33% for a sampling-and-filter baseline to 65%, and lowers MSE by over 20% relative to sampling-and-filter under the same search budget. These results establish EXPLORE as the first framework to integrate structured test-time search with LM decoding for analog topology generation, and a practical step toward scaling LLM-driven design automation.

AI.tldr: EXPLORE uses search-enhanced decoding with simulator-guided MCTS to scale LM-driven analog topology design, achieving higher success and lower MSE than one-shot or baseline methods.
AI.motivation: Automate analog circuit topology design to reduce manual effort and meet diverse, customized requirements; one-shot LM approaches struggle due to large search spaces and limited training data.
AI.method: Integrates simulator-guided Monte Carlo Tree Search with transformer-based decoding; leverages language-model priors; bypasses high-confidence structural tokens to focus simulator budget on topology-altering decisions.
AI.result: On a 6-component benchmark at a 0.01 tolerance, success rate rises from 12% (one-shot) and 33% (sampling baseline) to 65%; MSE is reduced by over 20% relative to sampling-and-filter under the same search budget.
AI.conclusion: First framework to integrate structured test-time search with LM decoding for analog topology generation; a practical step toward scalable LLM-driven design automation.

title: When Bots Join the Team: Bot Adoption and the Institutional Fabric of Open-Source Software Projects
summary: AI agents are joining human teams, raising a basic question: when an automated agent becomes a regular participant, does group organization strengthen or weaken? We study this question in open-source software, where bots open pull requests, review code, and merge changes alongside people, leaving a public record of every interaction. Treating bots as participants rather than tools, we examine 2,991 GitHub projects for two years before and after each adopted its first bot. We measure three capabilities that institutional theory links to durable coordination - repeated engagement, social memory, and role differentiation - and two outcomes: conflict cascades and output distinctiveness. Bot adoption is followed by more repeated collaboration, greater recognition of specific bots in discussion, fewer conflict cascades, and more distinctive outputs. These changes cluster around adoption rather than accumulating gradually. Because we lack an untreated comparison group, we interpret the results as precisely timed associations, not causal effects. Two patterns are difficult for alternative explanations to account for: capabilities predict outcomes according to their function - coordination versus differentiation - rather than whether humans or bots provide them, and human-side capabilities account for the bot-conflict association but not the bot-distinctiveness association. The findings are consistent with a specific interpretation: predictable, rule-based agents can become part of a community's social infrastructure. The bot is the occasion; social organization is the mechanism.

AI.tldr: Treats bots as participants in OSS projects; around bot adoption, projects show increased repeated collaboration, more bot identity in discussions, fewer conflict cascades, and more distinctive outputs; associations are time-specific, not proven causation; results align with institutional theory of coordination and social differentiation.
AI.motivation: Investigate how automated agents integrated as regular participants affect group organization, extending institutional theory to software development communities and testing whether bots strengthen or weaken coordination and social structure in open-source projects.
AI.method: Quasi-longitudinal, event-based analysis of 2,991 GitHub projects over two years around each project’s first bot adoption; measures three capabilities linked to durable coordination (repeated engagement, social memory, role differentiation) and two outcomes (conflict cascades, output distinctiveness); observational data with interpreted associations; acknowledges lack of untreated control group.
AI.result: Bot adoption is associated with more repeated collaboration, greater recognition of specific bots in discussion, fewer conflict cascades, and more distinctive outputs; effects cluster around adoption time; findings align with function-based predictions (coordination vs differentiation); human-side capabilities explain bot-conflict association but not bot-distinctiveness.
AI.conclusion: The results support the view that predictable, rule-based agents can become part of a community’s social infrastructure; bots articulate a social role within a team's coordination and differentiation dynamics; while associations are documented, causal inference remains limited without a control group.

title: TreeSRNF: Square-Root Normal Fields for Generative Modelling of the Geometric and Structural Variability in Tree-like 3D Objects
summary: We introduce a novel mathematical framework for analyzing and generating complex tree-shaped 3D objects, such as botanical trees and plants, which deform both in their 3D geometry and branching structure. Unlike previous works, which either consider only the skeletal structure of tree-like objects or approximate their 3D geometry using branch thickness, the proposed framework accurately models both the 3D geometry of the tree branches and the way they are interconnected. In this paper, we first generalize the Square Root Normal Fields (SRNF) representation, originally proposed for the statistical analysis of genus-0 surfaces, to tree-shaped 3D objects. We then treat tree-shaped 3D objects as points on a novel Riemannian tree-shape space equipped with a novel Riemannian metric that measures the amount of surface bending and stretching, and structural changes one needs to apply to one 3D tree-shape to align it with another. This way, deformations become trajectories in this novel tree-shape space. We analyze the theoretical properties of this novel tree-shape space and the corresponding metric and develop algorithms for computing point-wise and branch-wise correspondences and geodesic paths between complex 3D trees. We finally show how to use these building blocks for (1) computing statistical summaries, \ie means and modes of variation, of collections of tree-shaped 3D objects, and (2) synthesizing novel tree-shaped 3D objects by sampling from probability distributions fitted to a population of tree-shaped 3D objects. We demonstrate the performance and utility of the proposed framework on real and synthetic plants and botanical trees and show that it significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art.

AI.tldr: A generalized SRNF-based Riemannian framework for jointly modeling and generating tree-shaped 3D objects, integrating surface geometry and branching topology to compute correspondences, geodesics, and statistics for synthesis.
AI.motivation: Existing approaches focus on either skeletal structure or coarse geometry (branch thickness) and fail to jointly model 3D geometry and branching connectivity. A unified framework enables accurate deformation analysis, correspondence, and generation of tree-like objects.
AI.method: Extend Square Root Normal Fields (SRNF) to tree-shaped 3D objects and define a novel Riemannian tree-space with a metric accounting for surface bending, stretching, and structural changes. Develop algorithms for point-wise and branch-wise correspondences and compute geodesics. Use these to estimate means, modes of variation, and to sample distributions for synthesizing new tree-shaped objects.
AI.result: The paper analyzes theoretical properties of the tree-space, presents algorithms for correspondences and geodesics, and demonstrates improved performance over state-of-the-art on real and synthetic plants and botanical trees.
AI.conclusion: A unified, geometry-aware framework for analysis and generation of tree-shaped 3D objects that outperforms prior methods, with potential applications in botany, computer graphics, and biologically inspired design.

title: Layered Risk Mapping for Autonomous Patient Transport in Expeditionary Medical Facilities
summary: In expeditionary medical facilities, routine patient transport imposes a compounding burden of personal protective equipment consumption, staff diversion, and elevated infection risk that becomes unsustainable under surge conditions. While autonomous wheelchairs could absorb this operational load, the safety-critical nature of patient transit within these highly unstructured and dynamic environments poses complex navigational challenges. To address this, we present a layered risk mapping framework that fuses four heterogeneous environmental hazards (terrain slope, static and dynamic obstacles, and semantic traversability) into a unified probabilistic cost surface via a Noisy-OR fusion model. In a paired Monte-Carlo evaluation, risk-informed fusion reduces collision rates from over 73% to under 32% and more than doubles obstacle clearance relative to a risk-unaware baseline. Additionaly, Noisy-OR achieves the highest clearance to obstacles and the lowest conditional peak risk across all tested hazard densities. We further validate the framework on a commercial powered wheelchair across three representative mission profiles in indoor and outdoor deployments, demonstrating that this architecture successfully meets the planning requirements of this previously unaddressed operational regime.

AI.tldr: A four-hazard risk fusion framework using Noisy-OR to create a probabilistic cost surface for autonomous wheelchairs, validated by Monte Carlo simulations and real wheelchair tests, reducing collision risk and improving obstacle clearance.
AI.motivation: In expeditionary medical facilities, routine patient transport strains PPE, staff resources, and infection control; autonomous transport must navigate unstructured, dynamic environments safely, especially under surge conditions.
AI.method: Fuse terrain slope, static and dynamic obstacles, and semantic traversability into a unified probabilistic cost surface using a Noisy-OR fusion model; evaluate with paired Monte-Carlo simulations against a risk-unaware baseline; validate on a commercial powered wheelchair across indoor and outdoor mission profiles.
AI.result: Risk-informed fusion reduces collision rates from over 73% to under 32% and more than doubles obstacle clearance relative to a risk-unaware baseline; Noisy-OR achieves the highest clearance to obstacles and the lowest conditional peak risk across hazard densities.
AI.conclusion: The proposed layered risk mapping framework enables safer autonomous patient transport in complex environments and demonstrates viability for a previously unaddressed operational regime, with implications for PPE conservation and infection risk reduction during surge conditions.

title: OrDA: Orthogonal Disentanglement of Access Habits Framework for Homepage Marketing Block Recommendations
summary: Clicks on homepage marketing blocks are driven by a dual-mechanism of content interest and access habits. However, habitual clicks often create Pseudo-Positives in marketing slots, where position advantage masks mediocre content quality, leading to biased recommendation ecosystems. We propose a framework called Orthogonal Disentanglement of Access habits (OrDA) to purify interest signals. OrDA utilizes a dual-tower structure with a gated allocation layer to adaptively route features and minimize interference. To ensure rigorous separation, we employ orthogonal regularization to constrain the latent interest and habit manifolds to be geometrically perpendicular. OrDA performs causal intervention (do-calculus) during inference to rank items solely by purified interest scores. Empirical online evaluations on large-scale datasets demonstrate that OrDA effectively eliminates access-habit bias, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in predictive accuracy. Online AB test 5.64% shows user click-through rates (UCTR) improvement on the Zhima homepage marketing block, Zhima rent-floor recommendation.

AI.tldr: OrDA disentangles access habits from content interest to purify signals in homepage marketing blocks, using a dual-tower with gated allocation, orthogonal regularization, and do-calculus inference, yielding improved predictive accuracy and a 5.64% CTR uplift in online A/B tests.
AI.motivation: Clicks on homepage marketing blocks are driven by both content interest and habitual access. Habitual clicks create pseudo-positives where position advantage masks content quality, biasing recommendations. A method is needed to separate genuine interest from habitual bias to improve ranking and fairness.
AI.method: OrDA employs a dual-tower architecture with a gated allocation layer to adaptively route features and minimize interference between interest and habit signals. Orthogonal regularization enforces geometrical perpendicularity between latent interest and habit manifolds. During inference, do-calculus-based causal intervention ranks items by purified interest scores, suppressing access-habit influence.
AI.result: Empirical online evaluations on large-scale datasets show OrDA effectively eliminates access-habit bias and outperforms state-of-the-art methods in predictive accuracy. An online A/B test reports a 5.64% improvement in user click-through rate (UCTR) on Zhima homepage marketing blocks (Zhima rent-floor recommendation).
AI.conclusion: OrDA successfully purifies interest signals by disentangling access habits, yielding more accurate rankings and higher engagement in real-world deployments.

title: AgentCompass: A Unified Evaluation Infrastructure for Agent Capabilities
summary: As Large Language Models (LLMs) evolve into autonomous agents, the need for unified evaluation infrastructure becomes critical. However, current evaluation pipelines remain highly fragmented and tightly coupled, hindering reproducibility and causing redundant engineering. To address this, we introduce AgentCompass, an open-source, lightweight, and extensible infrastructure for evaluating LLM-based agents. AgentCompass organizes the evaluation process around three independent components, namely Benchmark, Harness, and Environment, thereby enabling flexible configurations without requiring the reimplementation of complex execution logic. Furthermore, it features a fault-tolerant asynchronous runtime and comprehensive trajectory analysis tools to transparently diagnose nuanced failure modes like reward-hacking. Natively supporting over 20 benchmarks across five capability dimensions, AgentCompass provides the community with a scalable and reproducible infrastructure for advancing agent research.

AI.tldr: AgentCompass is an open-source modular framework for evaluating LLM-based agents, introducing Benchmark, Harness, and Environment along with fault-tolerant runtime and trajectory analysis, supporting 20 benchmarks across five capability dimensions.
AI.motivation: To address fragmentation and low reproducibility in current evaluation pipelines for LLM agents.
AI.method: Modular architecture: Benchmark, Harness, Environment; asynchronous fault-tolerant runtime; trajectory analysis tooling; supports 20 benchmarks across five capabilities; open-source; designed for extensibility and reproducibility.
AI.result: Provides a scalable, reproducible evaluation infrastructure for agent research; enables flexible configurations without reimplementing execution logic; transparent diagnostics of failures such as reward-hacking.
AI.conclusion: AgentCompass offers a unified, extensible platform for rigorous evaluation of LLM-based agents, reducing engineering overhead and accelerating research progress.

title: 2D Rotary Position Embedding for Scene Text Recognition with Transformers
comment: 17 pages, 3 figures. Under review at the International Journal on Document Analysis and Recognition (IJDAR)
summary: Scene Text Recognition (STR) remains challenging due to the diversity of text appearances, including curvature, rotation, and perspective distortion. Recent Transformer-based approaches perform well but usually rely on one-dimensional positional encodings that ignore the 2D spatial structure of text images. Axial 2D extensions of Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) exist for vision Transformers, but they assume roughly square, isotropic image content and apply the rotation only within encoder self-attention. Scene text violates both assumptions: crops are markedly anisotropic, and STR models are encoder-decoder, so the decoder must relate its queries to the encoder's 2D layout through cross-attention. We introduce 2D-RoPE-STR, which adapts axial 2D-RoPE to this setting through (1) an anisotropic row/column dimension allocation matched to the aspect ratio of text, and (2) an extension of the rotary coupling into encoder-decoder cross-attention, letting autoregressive decoding steps attend to encoder tokens by their 2D layout, a setting not addressed by prior encoder-only formulations. Both changes are essentially parameter-free and require no architectural redesign beyond the positional-encoding module. We further introduce a diagnostic protocol (a controlled ablation pair isolating only the positional encoding, an image-level net-win disagreement analysis, and encoder attention visualization) that identifies where and why relative 2D position helps: curved, rotated, and perspective-distorted layouts where reading order departs from a straight horizontal line. On six standard benchmarks (IIIT5K, SVT, ICDAR 2013, ICDAR 2015, CUTE80, SVTP), gains concentrate on exactly these irregular layouts, with ablations isolating each design choice against 1D RoPE and 2D sinusoidal and learnable alternatives.

AI.tldr: 2D-RoPE-STR introduces anisotropic 2D Rotary Position Embeddings and extends rotary coupling to encoder-decoder cross-attention, enabling STR models to utilize 2D layout for irregular text and improving accuracy on curved/rotated/perspective-distorted scenes; diagnostic protocol isolates benefits.
AI.motivation: Scene Text Recognition suffers from non-2D-friendly transformations and anisotropic crops; existing axial RoPE works in encoder-only vision transformers but not for encoder-decoder STR with cross-attention; need 2D positional encoding that respects aspect ratio and cross-attention layout.
AI.method: Propose anisotropic allocation of row/column dimensions in 2D-RoPE matched to text aspect ratio; extend rotary coupling to cross-attention in encoder-decoder; maintain parameter-free approach; introduce diagnostic protocol (ablation, image-level disagreement, encoder attention visualization).
AI.result: On six benchmarks (IIIT5K, SVT, ICDAR 2013/2015, CUTE80, SVTP), gains concentrate on irregular layouts; ablations show superiority over 1D RoPE and 2D sinusoidal/learnable alternatives.
AI.conclusion: Relative 2D position encoding via anisotropic 2D-RoPE and cross-attention rotary coupling effectively leverages 2D layout in STR, with a diagnostic framework clarifying where benefits arise.

title: Improving Map Consistency in Graph-Based LiDAR SLAM Through Information-Aware Odometry and Retroactive Loop Closure
summary: High-quality maps are fundamental for robotics tasks such as navigation and planning. Although modern graph-based LiDAR SLAM systems achieve good trajectory accuracies, a low trajectory error alone does not guarantee geometrically consistent maps, particularly at revisit locations where missed loop closures and residual drift can produce local misalignments. In this work, we address the problem of jointly improving global trajectory estimation and local map quality in 3D LiDAR SLAM. We first propose a framework to efficiently estimate geometry-dependent information matrices for ICP, enabling principled weighting of odometry constraints in a pose graph. We then introduce a hierarchical loop-closure module that decouples place recognition from geometric registration, together with a retroactive loop-closure module that exploits the optimized pose graph to recover missed loop closures. We also propose an evaluation protocol to measure map consistency at revisit locations. We evaluate our SLAM system on several datasets against state-of-the-art LiDAR SLAM systems. Experimental results demonstrate global trajectory accuracies on par with or better than existing methods while consistently improving local geometric map consistency at revisit locations. These results suggest that coupling uncertainty-aware odometry with geometry-guided loop-closure refinement leads to more accurate trajectories and higher-quality maps.

AI.tldr: Jointly improve global trajectory and local 3D LiDAR map quality using geometry-aware weighting for ICP constraints, hierarchical and retroactive loop closures, and a revisit-map-consistency evaluation protocol; achieves competitive trajectories with better local map consistency.
AI.motivation: Low trajectory error does not guarantee geometric consistency at revisits due to missed loop closures and drift; a framework that couples pose-graph uncertainty with geometry-based refinements is needed.
AI.method: (1) Efficiently estimate geometry-dependent information matrices for ICP to weight odometry in a pose graph; (2) Hierarchical loop-closure module decoupling place recognition from geometric registration; (3) Retroactive loop-closure module leveraging the optimized pose graph to recover missed closures; (4) Evaluation protocol for map consistency at revisit locations.
AI.result: Global trajectory accuracy on par with or better than state-of-the-art LiDAR SLAM systems; consistent improvement in local geometric map consistency at revisit locations.
AI.conclusion: Uncertainty-aware odometry combined with geometry-guided loop-closure refinement yields more accurate trajectories and higher-quality maps.

title: Temperature Scaling Is Not Enough: Calibration Gaps Under Human Label Distributions
summary: Temperature scaling is the dominant post-hoc calibration method in modern deep learning. Its theoretical justification rests on an assumption that is rarely stated explicitly: that ground-truth labels are one-hot and deterministic. In practice, labels are frequently soft, crowd-sourced, or genuinely distributional, reflecting real disagreement among human annotators rather than annotation noise. We study whether temperature scaling retains its calibration properties when this assumption is violated, and whether any resulting degradation depends on model scale. Using CIFAR-10H and ChaosNLI, two publicly available datasets with human-annotated soft label distributions, we evaluate three model scales per modality under both hard one-hot and soft distributional label targets. Across all nine configurations we find a positive soft-label calibration gap: temperature scaling calibrated on hard labels consistently underperforms an oracle calibrated directly on soft labels, with Brier Score gaps ranging from 0.002 to 0.134. The gap grows monotonically with model scale in the vision domain and on the SNLI-derived split of ChaosNLI, and is substantially larger in the language domain (mean gap 0.079) than in vision (mean gap 0.003). A scale-ordering reversal on the MNLI-derived split remains after matched-domain training; we treat it as inconclusive for the scale hypothesis and attribute it primarily to near-chance accuracy on that split. As a second post-hoc baseline, multiclass isotonic regression yields the same qualitative conclusion: positive soft-label gaps in all nine configurations, and larger gaps in language than in vision. These findings suggest that calibration protocols built on majority-vote labels systematically misstate model reliability wherever label ambiguity is structural, with direct consequences for deployment in safety-critical settings.

AI.tldr: Hard-label calibration (temperature scaling) underestimates soft-label calibration; soft labels reveal systematic calibration gaps across model scales, larger in language than vision; isotonic regression yields similar gaps.
AI.motivation: Real-world labels are often soft or distributional due to annotator disagreement. It is unclear if temperature scaling remains calibrated when the one-hot assumption is violated, and whether this effect scales with model size.
AI.method: Empirical study on three model scales across two modalities (vision and language) using CIFAR-10H and ChaosNLI datasets with hard (one-hot) vs soft label targets; compare temperature scaling to an oracle calibrated on soft labels and to multiclass isotonic regression.
AI.result: Temperature scaling calibrated on hard labels underperforms when using soft labels, with Brier score gaps 0.002–0.134; gaps grow with model scale in vision and SNLI-derived ChaosNLI, and are larger in language (mean gap 0.079) than vision (0.003). Scale-ordering reversal on MNLI split is inconclusive. Isotonic regression exhibits the same qualitative gaps.
AI.conclusion: Calibration protocols based on majority-vote (hard labels) misstate model reliability where label ambiguity is structural, with significant implications for safety-critical deployment.

title: CAVA: Canonical Action Verification and Attestation for Runtime Governance of Agentic AI Systems
comment: 35 pages. Working paper on canonical action verification, runtime governance, semantic pattern detection, and approval-bound action receipts
summary:
Agentic AI systems increasingly act through heterogeneous runtimes: local coding hooks, SDK tools, browser automation, managed-agent traces, API gateways, and workflow engines. A single operational act such as publishing code, changing identity state, moving money, or exporting data may therefore be represented by many incompatible runtime records. This makes a basic governance question difficult to answer: what action was actually approved, what evidence binds the approval to execution, and can an independent verifier reproduce the same action identity later?
  This paper presents Canonical Action Verification and Attestation (CAVA), a runtime-semantics layer for converting heterogeneous agent activity into canonical runtime action objects. CAVA is positioned below Proof-Carrying Agent Actions (PCAA): PCAA defines the deployer-owned route-review-prove governance process, while CAVA defines the stable action object that process governs. The paper formalizes canonical action identity, semantic pattern detection, approval binding, receipt integrity, runtime-portable projection, and optional attestation substrates. We study a reference implementation through a 96-seed, 384-variant benchmark covering semantic equivalence, semantic separation, wrapper bypass, false-positive control, approval binding, receipt reproducibility, attestation tamper detection, runtime portability, semantic pattern detection, policy degradation, and Azure deployment drills. The contribution is a systems formulation of action-level canonicalization and policy-addressable semantic patterns as a necessary substrate for deployer-side AI governance.

AI.tldr: CAVA provides a runtime-semantics layer that converts heterogeneous agent actions into canonical action objects, enabling verifiable governance across diverse runtimes and evidence linkage from approval to execution; validated via a large benchmark; positions under PCAA as the stable action object substrate.
AI.motivation: Agentic AI systems operate across heterogeneous runtimes, making it hard to answer what action was approved and whether it can be independently verified later. A canonical, portable representation of actions and their approvals is needed for governance and auditability.
AI.method: Propose and formalize Canonical Action Verification and Attestation (CAVA), a runtime-semantics layer that produces canonical action objects. Formalize action identity, semantic pattern detection, approval binding, receipt integrity, and runtime-portable projection, with optional attestation substrates. Develop a reference implementation and evaluate via a 96-seed, 384-variant benchmark across dimensions like semantic equivalence, wrapper bypass, false positives, attestation tamper detection, and Azure deployment drills.
AI.result: Formalization of action-level canonicalization and policy-addressable semantic patterns, plus a reference implementation and extensive benchmark testing. Demonstrates reproducibility of action identity, tamper detection, and portability across runtimes, establishing CAVA as a necessary substrate for deployer-side AI governance.
AI.conclusion: CAVA provides a necessary, runtime-portable foundation for action governance in heterogeneous agent ecosystems and complements PCAA by standardizing action objects for verifiable approvals and audits.

title: LPM: Industrial-Scale Generative Video Restoration
summary: We present the Large Processing Model (LPM), a diffusion-based generative framework for photorealistic video restoration under complex, in-the-wild degradations. To our knowledge, LPM is the first generative video restoration model deployed at industrial scale. LPM addresses the diverse degradations in user-generated content (UGC) through a unified system encompassing large-scale data engineering, foundation-model training, and efficient inference. Its enhanced architecture, progressive training strategy, and temporal-pyramid inference mechanism jointly enable high-fidelity, temporally consistent restoration of arbitrarily long videos across the broad content distribution encountered on UGC platforms. LPM has been deployed in production at Kuaishou, where videos processed by the model account for approximately 45% of total viewing time, delivering consistent improvements across key quality-of-experience metrics. Beyond perceptual enhancement, LPM delivers substantial system-level benefits: at comparable perceptual quality, it reduces bitrate by 20% relative to Kuaishou's in-house codec, yielding annual bandwidth cost savings on the order of hundreds of millions. Its low serving cost also enables integration into products such as Kling, demonstrating that generative restoration can be practical, scalable, and cost-effective for large-scale video processing.

AI.tldr: A diffusion-based video restoration framework (LPM) designed for industrial-scale, in-the-wild degradations, achieving high-fidelity, temporally consistent restoration for long UGC videos and enabling substantial system-level gains (reduced bitrate, bandwidth savings) with production deployment at Kuaishou.
AI.motivation: Address the broad, diverse degradations in user-generated content and provide a scalable, cost-effective restoration solution suitable for industrial deployment, delivering both perceptual quality and operational efficiency.
AI.method: Introduce Large Processing Model (LPM), a diffusion-based generative framework augmented by enhanced architecture, progressive training, and temporal-pyramid inference. It leverages large-scale data engineering, foundation-model pretraining, and efficient inference to handle arbitrarily long videos and real-time-like production demands, proven in production at Kuaishou and integrated into Kling.
AI.result: Achieves high-fidelity and temporally consistent restoration for long videos; deployment covers about 45% of total viewing time; reduces bitrate by ~20% compared to in-house codec; implies annual bandwidth savings in the hundreds of millions; lower serving cost enables product-wide integration.
AI.conclusion: Generative restoration via LPM is practical and scalable for large-scale video processing, demonstrating the viability of diffusion-based video restoration in industry and delivering substantial QoE and system-level benefits.

title: Kepler-Encoder-v0.1: Towards a Multimodal Embedding Model for Robots
summary: A robot must understand the state of its own body, but a camera sees only part of it. Force and contact leave almost no trace in a single frame, and raw vision features read force at $R^2$ at or below $0.10$ on every robot we test. We present Kepler-Encoder-v0.1, a robot-first multimodal encoder that treats robot state as a modality and fuses vision, proprioception, and force/torque into a single shared latent with a learned-query cross-attention layer, trained self-supervised by masked cross-modal prediction under the LeJEPA/SIGReg objective. At evaluation only vision enters, which poses a sharp question. Does fusing state into training make the vision-only latent carry anything the pixels do not already contain? On the RH20T corpus the answer is yes, precisely where the camera is weakest. On held-out scenes, the vision-only latent recovers end-effector state, and force in particular, significantly above both raw frozen-ViT features and a compute-matched vision-only control on every sensored robot, though absolute force recovery at a single timestep is modest; on motor state, which the camera largely sees, it is statistically tied with the strongest vision baselines, and it is the only feature whose latent geometry tracks state. A single embodiment-agnostic encoder covers four robots, and a data-matched control shows this breadth reflects embodiment diversity rather than data volume. The frozen latent is directly useful. Its own cross-modal prediction error is a training-free invalid-state monitor (AUROC $0.90$ on out-of-range states, $0.69$ on scene-swapped states), and a diffusion decoder (PixNerd) reconstructs the camera frame from the latent, confirming the spatial compression preserves world-state. This report validates the single-timestep case; native-rate temporal fusion is the next step.

AI.tldr: Kepler-Encoder-v0.1 is a robot-first, multimodal encoder that fuses vision, proprioception, and force/torque into a single latent via learned-query cross-attention and self-supervised masked cross-modal prediction (LeJEPA/SIGReg). Evaluations show vision-only latent gains from training with state, recovering end-effector and force information beyond raw vision features, especially where the camera is weak; the encoder generalizes across four robots; a diffusion decoder reconstructs the camera frame, confirming spatial-state preservation; single-timestep results motivate future temporal fusion.
AI.motivation: Vision alone struggles to infer latent robot state, particularly for force/contact signals and parts of the body not visible to the camera. A robot-centric, multimodal latent could improve state estimation from visual input and enable better monitoring and control, even when vision is limited.
AI.method: A robot-first multimodal encoder creates a shared latent by fusing vision, proprioception, and force/torque using a learned-query cross-attention layer. Trained in self-supervised fashion via masked cross-modal prediction under the LeJEPA/SIGReg objective. Evaluation uses the RH20T corpus; only vision is used at test time. A diffusion decoder (PixNerd) reconstructs camera frames from the latent. A single embodiment-agnostic encoder is evaluated over four robots; cross-modal prediction error is used as a training-free invalid-state monitor.
AI.result: The vision-only latent, learned with state fusion, recovers end-effector state and force better than raw frozen-ViT features and a compute-matched vision baseline on held-out data, especially where the camera is weakest. Motor state remains comparable to strong baselines. The latent geometry tracks state across embodiments; the frozen latent supports a strong cross-modal predictive signal without training. The latent enables an AUROC of 0.90 for out-of-range states and 0.69 for scene-swapped states as an invalid-state monitor. PixNerd can reconstruct camera frames from the latent, confirming spatial-state preservation. The single-timestep results generalize across four robots; temporal fusion at native rates remains future work.
AI.conclusion: Fusing state information during training yields a vision-only latent that encodes additional state beyond pixels, particularly for weak camera views, and generalizes across embodiments. The latent is immediately useful for monitoring and state estimation, and spatial-state information is preserved in reconstruction. The study validates the single-timestep regime; extending to native-rate temporal fusion is the next step.

title: Data-Efficient Adaptation of LLMs via Attention Head Reweighting
summary: Learning effectively from limited data is critical in domains like security where labeled examples are scarce. Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated some capabilities for data-efficient learning, especially through parameter-efficient adaptation methods, but continue to struggle when faced with few samples for difficult tasks. To meet this challenge, we propose Attention Head Reweighting (AHR), a data-efficient method that adapts LLMs to new text-classification tasks by learning only a single scalar per attention head. This drastically reduces the number of parameters that need to be learned by making use of the functional specialization of individual attention heads. Experiments on diverse open-source text classification datasets show that AHR can outperform standard baselines like LoRA when learning from limited samples, despite having 200-1000x fewer trainable parameters, as our AHR only modifies ~0.0001% of the model's parameters. In addition, our learned weights are easy to interpret and can be analyzed to better understand the mechanisms and attention heads responsible for in-context learning abilities in LLMs.

AI.tldr: AHR is a parameter-efficient method that reweights attention heads with one scalar per head to improve data-efficient text classification, outperforming LoRA with far fewer trainable parameters; the approach is interpretable.
AI.motivation: To enable effective learning from very limited labeled data in LLMs by a highly parameter-efficient adaptation method that leverages the natural functional specialization of attention heads.
AI.method: Introduce Attention Head Reweighting (AHR): learn a single scalar per attention head to scale its contributions during task adaptation, with most model parameters frozen and only ~0.0001% of parameters adjusted.
AI.result: AHR outperforms standard baselines like LoRA on diverse open-source text classification datasets in few-shot settings, despite training 200–1000× fewer parameters; learned head weights are interpretable and reveal which heads contribute to in-context learning.
AI.conclusion: AHR offers a highly data- and parameter-efficient approach to adapting LLMs for text classification, providing interpretability and insights into the roles of individual attention heads in in-context learning.

title: Experience Memory Graph: One-Shot Error Correction for Agents
summary: Large Language Model (LLM) agents have shown remarkable capabilities in autonomous decision-making by generating sequential trajectories of states, actions, and observations. However, in complex, long-horizon tasks, these agents frequently suffer from compounding errors and struggle to recover from failures. Existing self-correction mechanisms rely on prompt-based reflection, which is inherently brittle, incurs heavy time and API costs due to iterative trial-and-error loops, and produces task-specific memory that may be hard to generalize to new scenarios. To address this, we propose Experience Memory Graph (EMG), a framework that reformulates agent failure recovery as a graph matching problem. At training time, we convert both failed exploration trajectories and successful expert trajectories into directed action decision graphs. By matching these graphs, we extract common subgraphs (successful workflows) and graph edit paths that explicitly indicate how to correct failures (e.g., which actions to add, delete, or relabel under a given observation), and store them in a memory graph with intra-task nodes and cross-task edges. At test time, EMG retrieves relevant insights and guides the agent in a single, loop-free execution. Experiments on ALFWorld and ScienceWorld show that EMG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art reflection baselines in success rate and average reward, while requiring no test-time trial-and-error.

AI.tldr: EMG reframes agent failure recovery as graph matching to build a reusable memory graph of corrective workflows, enabling loop-free test-time execution and improved performance over reflection baselines.
AI.motivation: LLM agents exhibit compounding errors in long-horizon tasks; prompt-based reflection is brittle, costly, and yields task-specific memory that generalizes poorly. There is a need for a general, efficient, test-time failure recovery mechanism.
AI.method: During training, convert failed exploration trajectories and successful expert trajectories into directed action decision graphs; perform graph matching to extract common subgraphs (successful workflows) and graph edit paths indicating how to fix failures (add/delete/relabel actions given observations); store these in a memory graph with intra-task nodes and cross-task edges. At test time, retrieve relevant insights from the memory graph to guide execution in a single, loop-free pass.
AI.result: EMG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art reflection baselines in both success rate and average reward on ALFWorld and ScienceWorld and requires no test-time trial-and-error.
AI.conclusion: Graph-based memory for failure recovery provides robust, generalizable, and efficient long-horizon planning for LLM agents, mitigating compounding errors without iterative trial-and-error.

title: HIVE-3D: Hierarchical Voxel Enhancement for High-Quality 3D Scene Generation
comment: Accepted at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2026). Project page: https://xbdff.github.io/HIVE-3D/
summary: Recently, a line of works can generate impressive 3D objects from a single image, but they are limited by restricted representation resolution, making them unsuitable for 3D scene generation. In this work, we introduce HIVE-3D, a novel method for high-quality 3D scene generation based on hierarchical voxel enhancement framework. Specifically, given a single scene image as input, we first produce a coarse initial scene, then introduce image segmentation and attention-based retrieval to align 2D image components with 3D scene components. Subsequently, we organize these scene relations into a hierarchical component tree, where nodes closer to the leaves denote finer-grained components. Finally, we propose a voxel super-resolution model that generates refined voxels for the target instance while maintaining strong consistency with the coarse voxels. Equipped with this model, we perform coarse-to-fine hierarchical super-resolution on images and voxels for each component, producing a high-resolution and high-quality 3D scene. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms previous approaches, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

AI.tldr: Hierarchical voxel enhancement (HIVE-3D) enables high-quality, high-resolution 3D scene generation from a single image by progressively refining voxels through a hierarchical component-tree and voxel super-resolution that preserves coherence with coarse geometry.
AI.motivation: Overcome the limited representation resolution in single-image 3D generation to enable scalable, high-quality 3D scene synthesis from monocular input.
AI.method: 1) Generate a coarse initial scene from a single image. 2) Use image segmentation and attention-based retrieval to align 2D image regions with 3D components. 3) Build a hierarchical component tree where leaves are finest components. 4) Propose a voxel super-resolution model to refine voxels for target instances while maintaining consistency with coarse voxels. 5) Perform coarse-to-fine hierarchical super-resolution on both images and voxels per component to produce high-res 3D scenes.
AI.result: Experimental results indicate strong performance, with the method significantly surpassing prior approaches and achieving state-of-the-art results on relevant benchmarks for single-image to 3D scene generation.
AI.conclusion: HIVE-3D demonstrates that a hierarchical voxel refinement framework, coupled with cross-modal alignment and multi-scale supervision, can produce high-quality, high-resolution 3D scenes from a single image, outperforming existing methods.

title: COLMAR: Cooperative View Policy Learning for Multi-Agent Active 3D Reconstruction
summary: Active 3D reconstruction requires selecting informative viewpoints under limited sensing budgets. In multi-agent settings, coordination inefficiencies such as redundant observations and spatial clustering can significantly reduce reconstruction quality. We present COLMAR, a cooperative view policy learning framework for multi-agent active 3D reconstruction. COLMAR formulates viewpoint allocation as a shared policy optimization over map-centric observations and introduces a reconstruction-aware objective that promotes overlap-aware coverage, team-level discovery, and collision-safe exploration. Dense feedback derived from incremental reconstruction updates aligns exploration behavior with downstream geometric quality. The policy is trained using parameter-sharing Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with independent per-agent action selection at deployment, conditioned on a fused team map and without inter-agent message passing for decision making. Selected viewpoints are then reconstructed with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) for high-fidelity photometric evaluation. Experiments on GLEAM and Replica demonstrate consistent improvements over heuristic and non-cooperative baselines, achieving up to 54% higher reconstruction accuracy and 49% greater coverage under matched sensing budgets.

AI.tldr: COLMAR is a cooperative multi-agent policy learning framework for active 3D reconstruction that uses a shared, map-centric PPO with per-agent actions, a reconstruction-aware objective (overlap-aware coverage, team discovery, collision-safe exploration), and dense reconstruction feedback; evaluated with 3D Gaussian Splatting on GLEAM/Replica, showing up to 54% higher reconstruction accuracy and 49% more coverage than baselines.
AI.motivation: To reduce coordination inefficiencies (redundant observations, spatial clustering) and improve reconstruction quality under limited sensing budgets in multi-agent active 3D reconstruction.
AI.method: Formulates viewpoint allocation as shared policy optimization over fused map-centric observations using parameter-sharing PPO. Independent per-agent actions at deployment, conditioned on a fused team map, with no inter-agent message passing. Introduces a reconstruction-aware objective promoting overlap-aware coverage, team-level discovery, and collision-safe exploration. Dense feedback from incremental reconstruction updates aligns exploration with downstream geometric quality. Viewpoints are evaluated via 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS).
AI.result: COLMAR achieves consistent improvements over heuristic and non-cooperative baselines on GLEAM and Replica, with up to 54% higher reconstruction accuracy and 49% greater coverage under matched sensing budgets.
AI.conclusion: Cooperative, map-centric policy learning with dense reconstruction feedback substantially enhances multi-agent active 3D reconstruction, reducing redundancy and improving geometric quality. Effective with simple deployment (independent actions) and no inter-agent messaging, validated on standard benchmarks; potential limitations include reliance on incremental feedback quality and generalization to diverse sensing conditions.

title: PUe: Biased Positive-Unlabeled Learning Enhancement by Causal Inference
comment: Extended arXiv version of the NeurIPS 2023 paper; includes additional discussion of related SAR-PU work
summary: Positive-Unlabeled (PU) learning aims to achieve high-accuracy binary classification with limited labeled positive examples and numerous unlabeled ones. Existing cost-sensitive-based methods often rely on strong assumptions that examples with an observed positive label were selected entirely at random. In fact, the uneven distribution of labels is prevalent in real-world PU problems, indicating that most actual positive and unlabeled data are subject to selection bias. Building on the SAR-PU propensity-weighted framework of Bekker et al., we study a PU learning enhancement (PUe) framework using normalized propensity scores and normalized inverse probability weighting (NIPW). PUe's main contributions are a normalized inverse-probability-weighted PU risk formulation; additional theoretical analyses of normalized sample-weight error and common PU estimators under biased labeling; regularized deep propensity-score estimation; integration with modern cost-sensitive PU methods; and support for selectively labeled negative classes. Experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and ADNI demonstrate improvements over several PU baselines under non-uniform label distributions.

AI.tldr: Proposes PUe: a normalized inverse probability weighted PU framework to handle biased labeling in PU learning, leveraging normalized propensity scores, regularized deep propensity estimation, and integration with cost-sensitive PU methods; shows theoretical insights and empirical gains on MNIST/CIFAR-10/ADNI under non-uniform label distributions.
AI.motivation: Address selection bias in PU data; existing methods assume random labeling, which is often violated in practice.
AI.method: Introduce PUe within SAR-PU, use normalized propensity scores (NPS) and normalized IPW (NIPW) for PU risk; provide theoretical analysis on sample-weight error; regularized deep propensity-score estimation; integration with modern cost-sensitive PU methods; support selectively labeled negatives.
AI.result: Empirical improvements over several PU baselines on MNIST, CIFAR-10, ADNI under non-uniform label distributions; theoretical analyses included.
AI.conclusion: Normalized propensity weighting and normalization improve PU learning under biased labeling, enabling better performance and compatibility with existing cost-sensitive PU approaches.

title: AIMO Interpretability Challenge
summary: We propose the AIMO Interpretability Challenge, a competition on distinguishing robust from spurious reasoning in frontier mathematical language models based on the models' internal mechanisms. The challenge is motivated by a central limitation of standard reasoning benchmarks: strong final-answer accuracy does not reveal whether a model relies on stable reasoning mechanisms or exploits brittle reasoning shortcuts. Building on AI Mathematical Olympiad (AIMO) problems and submissions, together with resources from the Fields Model Initiative, the competition will provide (1) newly-published olympiad-level math reasoning problems and their symbolic representations, allowing generation of novel functional variants, (2) access to frontier reasoning models, and (3) assessments of models' adversarial robustness on these problems. Participants will use these resources, along with our computing infrastructure support, to develop methods for identifying which models solve problems robustly. Our competition will also create a new, open robustness benchmark and baseline systems, aiming to provide a lasting foundation for standard benchmarking in mathematical reasoning and interpretability. Scientifically, the competition connects interpretability and generalization research around a central question in AI research: can we determine if, and to what extent, the decision-making of frontier AI models is generalizable and thus, reliable?

AI.tldr: AIMO Interpretability Challenge proposes a competition to distinguish robust from spurious reasoning in frontier mathematical language models by analyzing internal mechanisms, leveraging AIMO problems and Fields resources to create an open robustness benchmark and baselines, and to assess generalizability of models' decision-making.
AI.motivation: Standard reasoning benchmarks reveal final-answer accuracy but not whether the model uses stable, generalizable reasoning or brittle shortcuts; there is a need to link interpretability with generalization and reliability in frontier AI models.
AI.method: Build on AI Mathematical Olympiad (AIMO) problems and submissions and Fields Model Initiative resources to (1) publish olympiad-level math reasoning problems with symbolic representations for generating variants, (2) provide access to frontier reasoning models, and (3) assess adversarial robustness on these problems. Participants use computing infrastructure to develop methods for identifying which models solve problems robustly.
AI.result: The competition aims to yield a new open robustness benchmark and baseline systems, offering a lasting foundation for standard benchmarking in mathematical reasoning and interpretability.
AI.conclusion: Scientifically, it addresses a central AI research question: to what extent is the decision-making of frontier AI models generalizable and therefore reliable, by evaluating robustness and interpretability in mathematical reasoning tasks.

title: Bring Music The Horizon: Music-Driven 360$^\circ$ Video Generation
summary: Music visualization offers a powerful way to enhance listeners' understanding and experience of music by translating auditory signals into visual forms. However, most existing approaches either rely heavily on lyrics or generate flat, non-immersive videos similar to conventional music videos, which limits their ability to convey the emotional dynamics of music and provide an immersive listening experience. We propose Bring Music The Horizon, an emotion-aware pipeline for music-driven 360$^\circ$ video generation. Given an input song, our work first estimates its emotional trajectory by predicting valence-arousal values at the level of every four bars. These values are then converted into emotion-aware visual guidance using EmotiCrafter, and these guidance vectors can be manipulated by the SEGA framework, which provides fine-grained semantic control for keyframe generation. Finally, image-to-video models are applied to the generated keyframes to synthesize temporally continuous 360$^\circ$ videos for immersive music visualization. Our pipeline generates 360$^\circ$ music visualization videos that reflect the emotional progression and temporal structure of the input song. We demonstrate its capability using songs from different genres and provide qualitative comparisons with From-Sound-To-Sight, a representative audio-to-visual generation baseline, on our project page at https://etoile-et-toi-mp3.github.io/BMTH_Project_Page/.

AI.tldr: An end-to-end pipeline for emotion-aware 360° music visualization called Bring Music The Horizon (BMTH) that converts a song's valence-arousal trajectory into 360° video guidance via EmotiCrafter, controllable by SEGA for keyframe generation, and synthesized by image-to-video models, with qualitative baselines against From-Sound-To-Sight.
AI.motivation: Current music visualization methods either rely on lyrics or produce non-immersive visuals, failing to convey emotional dynamics and immersion. BMTH aims to capture the musical emotional trajectory and translate it into immersive 360° video with controllable visual semantics.
AI.method: 1) Estimate emotional trajectory by predicting valence-arousal every four bars. 2) Convert trajectory into emotion-aware visual guidance using EmotiCrafter. 3) Use SEGA for fine-grained semantic control of keyframe generation. 4) Apply image-to-video models to synthesize temporally coherent 360° videos from keyframes.
AI.result: BMTH generates 360° music visualization videos that reflect the emotional progression and temporal structure of the input song. Demonstrated on songs from multiple genres with qualitative comparisons against From-Sound-To-Sight; project page provided for evaluation.
AI.conclusion: The pipeline offers an end-to-end framework for emotion-aware, immersive music visualization with controllable semantics and temporal coherence, demonstrating cross-genre applicability; future work could include quantitative user studies and more rigorous evaluation of emotion alignment and generalization.

title: Flow-aware Optimal Navigation in Unsteady Flows through Reinforcement Learning
summary: Autonomous robotic navigation in nonstationary time-varying fluid flows remains a fundamental challenge due to partial observability and the unpredictability of realistic environments. While classical optimal control frameworks employed in robotics require unrealistic a-priori global flow knowledge, biological systems are able to navigate successfully by exploiting localized sensory cues. In this work we present a reinforcement learning approach using the TD3 algorithm to train autonomous agents to reach arbitrary targets within a parametric, chaotic double-gyre flow. To investigate optimal sensory mechanisms, we evaluate five bio-inspired observation strategies based on relative position, local velocity or local vorticity measures, and short-term memory variants. Additionally, we analyze the impact of providing agents with explicit global flow parameters. Numerical results demonstrate that an agent that is able to sense and remember a set number of flow velocity measures achieves the highest performance. The experiments reveal a trade-off in sensor utility: velocity-aware agents optimize energy efficiency, whereas vorticity sensors provide superior structural mapping and achieve better target proximity. Incorporating explicit global flow parameters is shown to decrease navigation performance. This behavior suggests that reinforcement learning-based autonomous systems develop more robust and general policies when restricted to implicit flow representations. The presented results offer insights for improving the transition of bio-inspired robotic navigation from simulation to real-world environments.

AI.tldr: TD3-based reinforcement learning enables autonomous navigation in a chaotic double-gyre flow; memory-enabled velocity sensing yields best performance; global flow parameters reduce performance.
AI.motivation: Address partial observability and nonstationarity in fluid-flow navigation; evaluate bio-inspired sensing strategies to bridge simulation–real-world transfer.
AI.method: Train agents with TD3 in a parametric chaotic double-gyre flow; evaluate five bio-inspired observation strategies (relative position, local velocity, local vorticity, plus two short-term memory variants); compare with explicit global flow parameters.
AI.result: Memory-enabled velocity sensing achieves the highest performance; velocity sensors favor energy efficiency; vorticity sensors enhance mapping and target proximity; providing explicit global flow parameters degrades performance.
AI.conclusion: RL with implicit flow representations yields robust, general policies for navigation in time-varying flows; findings inform sensor design and facilitate sim-to-real transfer.

title: Discrete Diffusion Models: A Unified Framework from Tokenization to Generation
summary: Discrete denoising diffusion models (DDMs) have recently emerged as a compelling alternative to autoregressive (AR) modeling for discrete data, offering parallel generation and iterative global refinement capabilities. Unlike continuous diffusion, where the state space is fixed, DDMs are fundamentally shaped by how the discrete state space is constructed: the tokenization scheme, the vocabulary topology, and domain-specific structural alphabets. This work introduces a unified conceptual framework that views discrete diffusion models through the construction of the underlying discrete state space. Within this framework, existing formulations, including transition-matrix, masking/absorbing-state, and score/ratio-based approaches, emerge as different instantiations of a common design space. The framework further exposes common design trade-offs across training objectives, inference algorithms, scaling behavior, systems optimization, and evaluation protocols, suggesting several promising directions for future research.

AI.tldr: Unifies discrete diffusion models by treating the discrete state space (tokenization, topology, alphabets) as the design space; shows existing DDM formulations are instantiations within this space; outlines training, inference, scaling, and evaluation trade-offs and future directions.
AI.motivation: To provide a coherent framework that explains how discrete state-space construction shapes DDM behavior and connects different methodological families (transition-matrix, masking/absorbing-state, score/ratio-based).
AI.method: Conceptual framework mapping discrete diffusion approaches to common design space, analyzing implications for training objectives, inference algorithms, scalability, systems optimization, and evaluation protocols.
AI.result: Demonstrates that diverse discrete DDM formulations can be viewed as instantiations within a single design space; identifies trade-offs and potential directions for standardized evaluation and future research.
AI.conclusion: A unified state-space perspective clarifies design choices, facilitates cross-method insights, and guides future research in tokenization, topology, and alphabets for improved discrete diffusion modeling.

title: A Self-Evolving Agent for Longitudinal Personal Health Management
comment: 20 pages, 4 figures, 6 supplementary tables. Code: https://github.com/HC-Guo/HealthClaw
summary: Personal health management unfolds over repeated encounters, yet most health AI systems treat each request in isolation. We developed HealthClaw, an open-source agent architecture that updates support as a person's routines, preferences, measurements and risks change. It separates shared safety rules and medical knowledge from private longitudinal memory containing profile facts, reusable procedures and episodic traces. After each episode, induction determines what should update the profile, revise a procedure, remain episodic or be excluded. We evaluated HealthClaw with a synthetic year-long benchmark and nine 200-case biomedical tasks. Across 900 longitudinal support probes, answer accuracy increased from 0.2% with current-query prompting to 45.7% with HealthClaw, while prompt-side context exposure was 71.7% lower than with full-history prompting. In 100 privacy probes, HealthClaw produced higher privacy-aware answer quality and fewer unsafe disclosures than both baselines. Across the biomedical tasks, the mean absolute gain in the task-specific primary metric was 27.0 percentage points, and seven gains remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction. These offline benchmarks support governed, self-evolving memory for longitudinal personal health agents, although clinical effectiveness requires prospective evaluation. HealthClaw is publicly available at https://github.com/HC-Guo/HealthClaw.

AI.tldr: HealthClaw is an open-source agent architecture for longitudinal personal health management that maintains private memory and updates it across episodes, improving task accuracy and privacy vs baselines; demonstrated offline with synthetic benchmarks and nine 200-case tasks; prospective clinical evaluation needed.
AI.motivation: Address the need for memory-enabled, privacy-preserving health AI that can evolve its behavior over time as a person’s routines, measurements, and risks change, rather than treating requests in isolation.
AI.method: Architecture separates shared safety rules and medical knowledge from private longitudinal memory (profile facts, reusable procedures, episodic traces). After each episode, induction decides what updates to perform (profile, procedure, episodic, or exclusion). Evaluated on a synthetic year-long benchmark and 9 tasks (900 probes, 100 privacy probes). Compared to prompts with current-history, HealthClaw improves answer accuracy and reduces prompt exposure; shows higher privacy-aware quality and fewer unsafe disclosures.
AI.result: Across 900 longitudinal probes, accuracy rose from 0.2% (current-query prompting) to 45.7% with HealthClaw; prompt exposure reduced by 71.7% vs full-history prompting. Privacy probes showed higher privacy-aware quality and fewer unsafe disclosures than baselines. Across 9 biomedical tasks, mean absolute gain in the primary metric = 27.0 percentage points; seven gains remained significant after FDR correction. HealthClaw publicly available at the provided GitHub URL.
AI.conclusion: Offline benchmarks support governing, self-evolving memory for longitudinal personal health agents. Clinical effectiveness requires prospective evaluation.

title: GPOcc++: Unified Sparse Gaussian Occupancy Prediction with Visual Geometry Priors
summary: Accurate 3D scene understanding is fundamental to embodied intelligence and autonomous driving, where 3D occupancy provides a unified representation of objects, structures, and free space. However, recovering such a complete volumetric representation from visual observations remains challenging, particularly in occluded and unobserved regions. Visual geometry priors offer strong and generalizable geometric cues for addressing this challenge, but their outputs are inherently surface-centric, whereas occupancy prediction requires reasoning about volumetric interiors and free space. To bridge this gap, we introduce GPOcc, which transforms visual geometry priors into occupancy-aware sparse Gaussian representations for efficient and expressive volumetric scene modeling. Building on GPOcc, GPOcc++ models multi-view observations and temporal sequences within a unified framework, allowing spatial and temporal evidence to be handled through the same representation. We further extend GPOcc++ from indoor scenes to outdoor occupancy prediction. Extensive experiments on both indoor and outdoor benchmarks demonstrate consistently strong performance across both multi-view and temporal settings, together with favorable efficiency and generalization. Code will be released at https://github.com/JuIvyy/GPOcc.

AI.tldr: Introduces GPOcc, a method to convert visual geometry priors into occupancy-aware sparse Gaussian representations for volumetric scene modeling, extended to GPOcc++ for multi-view and temporal data, and outdoors with strong accuracy, efficiency, and generalization.
AI.motivation: To recover a complete volumetric (occupied/free) representation from visual inputs, addressing the limitations of surface-centric priors in occupancy prediction, especially under occlusion and unobserved regions.
AI.method: Transform visual geometry priors into occupancy-aware sparse Gaussian representations. GPOcc++ unifies multi-view observations and temporal sequences within the same representation, enabling simultaneous spatial and temporal reasoning. Extension to outdoor occupancy prediction.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on indoor and outdoor benchmarks show strong performance across multi-view and temporal settings, with favorable efficiency and generalization. Code to be released.
AI.conclusion: GPOcc/GPOcc++ provide a principled, efficient framework to convert geometry priors into volumetric occupancy predictions, achieving robust indoor/outdoor generalization and unified handling of spatial-temporal evidence.

title: IMMNet: Hybrid Fusion of Model-based and Data-driven Approaches for Maneuvering Target Tracking
summary: Maneuvering target tracking in three-dimensional space remains a challenging problem due to complex motion dynamics and model mismatch. To address this, this paper proposes a hybrid model/data-driven algorithm named IMMNet, which integrates the interpretable structure of the interacting multiple model (IMM) algorithm with learnable neural components. Unlike end-to-end black-box methods, the proposed IMMNet algorithm not only can preserve the Bayesian inference mechanism that is essential for real-time radar applications, but also can adaptively learn motion patterns and noise characteristics from data. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed IMMNet algorithm consistently outperforms the existing algorithms across various scenarios, validating it as a robust, interpretable, and practical solution for maneuvering target tracking.

AI.tldr: A hybrid IMMNet approach that combines the Interacting Multiple Model (IMM) framework with neural components to enhance 3D maneuvering target tracking, preserving Bayesian inference for real-time radar while learning motion and noise patterns from data.
AI.motivation: To address complex 3D maneuvering dynamics and model mismatch in target tracking, balancing interpretability and performance with real-time Bayesian tracking.
AI.method: A hybrid model/data-driven algorithm (IMMNet) that integrates the IMM structure with learnable neural components, preserving the Bayesian update while adaptively learning motion patterns and noise characteristics from data (not a fully end-to-end black-box model).
AI.result: Experimental results indicate that IMMNet consistently outperforms existing algorithms across diverse scenarios, demonstrating robustness, interpretability, and practicality for maneuvering target tracking.
AI.conclusion: IMMNet provides a robust and interpretable bridge between model-based IMM and data-driven learning, delivering improved performance for 3D maneuvering target tracking while maintaining real-time Bayesian inference.

title: Local Redundancy: An Information-Theoretic Measure of Plasticity from Synthetic Memorization
summary: Plasticity -- a neural network's ability to adapt to new tasks -- is critical for continual and transfer learning. Existing measures, such as effective rank, dead neuron fraction, and weight norm, lack theoretical grounding and correlate poorly with performance on new tasks. We introduce local redundancy, an information-theoretic measure derived from universal compression theory. We define local redundancy as the worst-case redundancy of a local model family -- parameters in an infinitesimal neighborhood along gradient directions -- and show this is a principled measure of plasticity. Although local redundancy is intractable to compute exactly, we prove that the expected squared gradient norm on a synthetic memorization task provides an efficiently computable lower bound. Experiments on continual image classification and time series transfer learning demonstrate that local redundancy predicts downstream performance better than existing measures and enables pretraining checkpoint selection where validation loss plateaus.

AI.tldr: Local redundancy is a principled, information-theoretic measure of neural plasticity, capturing how much a model can adapt locally in parameter space; it serves as a computable proxy for downstream transfer performance and helps select pretrained checkpoints.
AI.motivation: Current plasticity measures (e.g., effective rank, dead neurons, weight norms) lack theoretical grounding and poorly predict transfer performance. A rigorous, computable criterion is needed to quantify a model’s capacity to adapt to new tasks.
AI.method: Define local redundancy as the worst-case redundancy of a local model family formed by infinitesimal parameter changes along gradient directions. Ground the concept in universal compression theory. Prove that exact computation is intractable, but derive a computable lower bound via the expected squared gradient norm on a synthetic memorization task. Validate with continual image classification and time-series transfer learning experiments, comparing to existing measures.
AI.result: Local redundancy correlates better with downstream performance than existing metrics and enables effective pretraining checkpoint selection, especially in regimes where validation loss plateaus, outperforming traditional plasticity measures.
AI.conclusion: Local redundancy provides a theoretically grounded, computable measure of plasticity rooted in information theory, with practical utility for predicting transfer performance and guiding pretraining decisions.

title: Do Agent Optimizers Compound? A Continual-Learning Evaluation on Terminal-Bench 2.0
summary: Most reported gains from agent-optimization methods are one-shot: an agent is optimized against a fixed benchmark and the resulting improvement is reported as if it were a stable property of the method. This does not test the setting that matters for deployed agents, where optimization is applied recursively as new failures and new tasks appear over time. The central question this raises is whether optimizer-driven gains compound: after an agent has been optimized once, can it be optimized again on newly arrived tasks without eroding the gains the first round produced? We study this question with a two-phase continual-learning evaluation built from hard tasks in Terminal-Bench 2.0, comparing three approaches to agent-harness optimization (GEPA, Meta Harness, and RELAI's Verifiable Continual Learning, RELAI-VCL) under identical optimization budgets. All three methods improve over the baseline agent in the conventional, static, single-phase setting. However, once new tasks are introduced, the methods diverge sharply: GEPA's optimized agent transfers below the unoptimized baseline, Meta Harness transfers well but fails to improve further once given a second optimization budget, and RELAI-VCL is the only method that both transfers positively to unseen tasks and continues improving after those tasks are folded into the optimization objective, reaching the highest pass rate at every evaluated stage and the highest lifelong average pass rate overall (76.4% vs. 66.0% for GEPA, 64.6% for Meta Harness, and 58.7% for the baseline). Our key observation was that optimization gains compounded only when regression control was built into the optimization loop, providing an inductive bias against shortcut solutions that fail to generalize.

AI.tldr: In continual optimization of agents, gains from a single optimization do not automatically accumulate across new tasks. The paper compares GEPA, Meta Harness, and RELAI-VCL in a two-phase continual-learning setup and finds only RELAI-VCL consistently improves and transfers to unseen tasks, suggesting regression control as a crucial inductive bias to prevent shortcut solutions and achieve lasting gains.
AI.motivation: Current evaluations of agent optimization are predominantly one-shot and respond to fixed benchmarks. This work asks whether optimizer-driven gains compound under continual task arrivals and whether optimization can improve on new tasks without eroding previous gains.
AI.method: Two-phase continual-learning evaluation using hard tasks from Terminal-Bench 2.0. Three optimization-harness methods (GEPA, Meta Harness, RELAI-VCL) are compared under identical budgets. Metrics include transfer to unseen tasks and lifelong average pass rate across stages.
AI.result: All three methods outperform the static baseline in the single-phase setting. Under new tasks, RELAI-VCL uniquely transfers positively to unseen tasks and continues improving, achieving the highest pass rates at each stage (e.g., lifelong average 76.4% vs. GEPA 66.0%, Meta Harness 64.6%, baseline 58.7%). GEPA degrades below baseline after adaptation; Meta Harness improves but does not further gain with a second optimization budget.
AI.conclusion: Optimization gains compound only when regression control is integrated into the optimization loop, providing an inductive bias against shortcut solutions that fail to generalize across evolving tasks.

title: CASA-SDF: Curriculum-Aware Spatial Adaptation with Curvature-Guided Density for Neural Implicit Surface Reconstruction
summary: Neural implicit representations have emerged as a powerful paradigm for 3D reconstruction. However, high-fidelity indoor surface reconstruction remains a significant challenge, primarily due to the pronounced \emph{geometric heterogeneity} of indoor scenes. Large texture-less planar regions typically require stronger regularization to suppress high-frequency artifacts, while thin structures demand sharper, more adaptive representations to mitigate the spectral bias of multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) and prevent over-smoothing. Existing approaches often rely on spatially indiscriminate prior supervision and a scene-global SDF-to-density transformation, which constrains their ability to balance planar smoothness and detail preservation.
