AI.conclusion: Expanded-rank ternary decomposition enables near-bf16 performance with ternary factors, with controllable memory/compute and sparsity; practical accuracy targets can be met exactly without rounding to coarser bit widths; competitive results on contemporary LLMs indicate strong potential for post-training quantization.

title: Nexus: Native Mesh Generation with Diffusion
summary: Generating high-quality triangle meshes is essential for film, gaming, and interactive 3D applications. Mainstream methods rely on mesh serialization and autoregressive processes, which stuggles in effective inference and is sensitive to error accumulation. In this paper, we present Nexus, a diffusion method that achieves holistic mesh generation via decoupled vertex and topology generation. First, we view mesh vertices as sparse voxels organized as an octree and adopt a diffusion model to generate the vertices in a coarse-to-fine manner. Second, for topology modeling, we propose Spacetime Interval, as an extension of Spacetime Distance to encode arbitrary edge and face topology into continuous per-vertex embeddings. It allows for a global and efficient recovery of complex topology. We then employ a diffusion model to generate the continuous embeddings on the generated vertices. Extensive experiments on the Objaverse and Toys4K datasets and in-the-wild images demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art autoregressive and two-stage baselines, effectively circumventing the inherent limitations of sequential mesh modeling. A blind user study from 3D practitioners confirms strong perceptual preference for our results.

AI.tldr: Nexus is a diffusion-based framework for holistic 3D mesh generation that decouples vertex and topology generation, using octree-based sparse voxels for vertex diffusion and a Spacetime Interval embedding to learn topology, achieving state-of-the-art results with perceptual validation.
AI.motivation: Current mesh generation methods rely on autoregressive/serialized meshes, which suffer from inference inefficiency and error accumulation, hindering scalable and accurate topology handling. There is a need for a holistic, topology-aware, diffusion-based approach.
AI.method: 1) Represent mesh vertices as sparse voxels organized in an octree and apply a diffusion model to generate vertices in coarse-to-fine steps. 2) Introduce Spacetime Interval, an extension of Spacetime Distance, to encode arbitrary edge/face topology into continuous per-vertex embeddings. 3) Use a diffusion model to generate these continuous embeddings on the generated vertices to recover topology globally.
AI.result: Empirical results on Objaverse, Toys4K, and in-the-wild images show Nexus outperforms state-of-the-art autoregressive and two-stage baselines, mitigating limitations of sequential mesh modeling. A blind user study with 3D practitioners reports strong perceptual preference for Nexus outputs.
AI.conclusion: A decoupled diffusion-based pipeline for mesh generation, combining voxel-structured vertex diffusion with topology-aware continuous embeddings, yields robust, high-quality meshes with improved inference and generalization over existing autoregressive methods.

title: Towards a Modular Bin-picking Framework for Handling Object Pose Uncertainties
comment: 7 pages, 5 figures, 1 table, keywords: bin picking; object manipulation; grasping strategies; object pose distribution estimation
summary:
In recent years, there has been growing interest in robust robotic systems for precise bin-picking applications. To achieve reliable performance, such systems must address errors arising from both the object pose estimation and the grasping process. Although various approaches have been proposed, they typically target specific challenges and do not offer general solutions. In this paper, we present a modular framework that jointly handles both error types. The framework incorporates object pose distribution estimation to account for pose uncertainty, which frequently arises in situations with ambiguous observations where a single correct pose cannot be determined. To further reduce uncertainty, we introduce a second-viewpoint module that computes complementary pose distributions, which are subsequently fused. This fusion decreases overall uncertainty and improves system efficiency. Additionally, two independent modules are included to compensate for grasping errors. The modular design allows the components to be combined for optimal performance or used individually, depending on the physical setup.
  The proposed method is evaluated in a real-world setup with three different objects, with no errors, and all modules are shown to improve efficiency. These results suggest that incorporating pose distributions with grasping pose errors is a promising direction for developing more flexible and reliable robotic production systems.
  To the best of our knowledge, this is the first framework that jointly addresses both grasping and object pose uncertainties using interchangeable modules. We believe there is ample opportunity to integrate additional modules, resulting in improved performance and flexibility. The current framework is limited to pose uncertainties in SO(2), but it could be extended to SE(3), enabling additional modules to improve the system.

AI.tldr: A modular framework for robust bin-picking that jointly handles pose uncertainty and grasping errors via pose distribution estimation, multi-view fusion, and grasping-error modules; validated on real-world experiments with three objects showing efficiency gains; extensible from SO(2) to SE(3).
AI.motivation: To address the combined challenges of object pose estimation uncertainty and grasping errors in robotic bin-picking, moving beyond methods that tackle only a single issue by offering a flexible, modular solution.
AI.method: Introduce a modular framework with: (1) object pose distribution estimation to model pose uncertainty; (2) a second-viewpoint module generating complementary pose distributions and fusion to reduce uncertainty; (3) two independent modules compensating grasping errors; components are interchangeable and combinable; currently scoped to pose uncertainty in SO(2), with potential extension to SE(3).
AI.result: Real-world experiments over three objects show that all modules improve efficiency; the framework jointly addressing grasping and pose uncertainties is the first of its kind and promising for flexible, reliable robotics; results suggest extending to SE(3) for broader applicability.
AI.conclusion: A flexible, modular approach that jointly tackles pose and grasping uncertainties; enables integration of additional modules and extension to SE(3), offering a path toward more robust robotic production systems.

title: Clustering algorithms for multivariate wind farm SCADA data filtering
summary: During wind farm operation, Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems record numerous anomalies, transients, and specific operational modes, leading to large datasets. However, for a wide range of applications, only measurements corresponding to normal operation are required and, therefore, the SCADA data must be filtered. For this purpose, several methods have been proposed to automate and replace manual filtering conducted by experts via visual inspection of the data. In this paper, we compare the filtering accuracy of multiple clustering algorithms against manual filtering, introducing evaluation metrics that are suitable for unlabeled data and robust across potential applications. Based on the results, we provide recommendations for generalizing model calibration to different datasets and discuss potential use cases for each model. The models are applied to the SCADA data of three turbines of an existing offshore wind farm, using 10-minute statistics across multiple data channels. In addition to the anomalies and operational modes typically recorded, the dataset presents a large number of non-evident outliers due to several field tests. Overall, the results highlight the importance of extending the analysis beyond the power curve, both in feature selection and in the design of evaluation metrics. In most cases, cluster-based methods are able to detect both evident and subtle outliers, achieving higher accuracy than manual filtering. However, the accuracy and the amount of data retained vary considerably depending on the model, and expert involvement remains necessary, though to a reduced extent compared to manual filtering.

AI.tldr: Cluster-based filtering of SCADA data for wind-farm operation; achieves higher accuracy than manual filtering in detecting outliers, but results vary by model; reduces expert effort though some calibration remains necessary.
AI.motivation: Automate filtering of unlabeled SCADA data to retain normal-operation measurements, capture both evident and subtle outliers, and generalize calibration across datasets.
AI.method: Apply multiple clustering algorithms to 10-minute statistical features from several SCADA channels across three offshore wind turbines; use metrics suitable for unlabeled data to evaluate against manual filtering; test on data with field-test outliers and non-evident anomalies; analyze beyond the power curve for feature selection and evaluation design.
AI.result: Cluster-based methods generally detect both evident and subtle outliers and outperform manual filtering in accuracy in many cases; however performance and data retention vary by model, and expert involvement is still required to some extent.
AI.conclusion: Extends data filtering assessment beyond the power curve; emphasizes careful feature selection and robust, unlabeled-evaluation metrics; provides guidance on calibrating models for different datasets and outlines model-specific use cases and trade-offs.

title: GHR-VLM: Making Zero-Shot Transit Video Analytics Realizable with Grounded Hybrid Reasoning
summary: Transit video understanding can provide valuable fine-grained data that conventional passenger counters and fare systems cannot capture. However, supervised video models require task-specific annotations, while applying vision-language models (VLMs) directly to long onboard videos is unreliable and costly. To leverage the complementary strengths of both approaches, we propose GHR-VLM, a visual grounded hybrid reasoning framework for zero-shot transit-bus video analytics. It is motivated by the observation that explicit visual grounding can improve VLM reasoning by converting long surveillance streams into compact, passenger-centered spatiotemporal evidence. Specifically, we propose an edge-cloud design in which a lightweight edge-based monitor continuously tracks door status and segments passenger clips. A backend VLM then identifies boarding passengers and classifies payment behavior through a two-stage coarse-to-fine refinement of spatiotemporal evidence. By invoking the VLM only on grounded passenger clips and contact sheets, GHR-VLM reduces cloud inference, avoids payment-specific training data, and supplies the localized evidence that VLMs otherwise struggle to identify. Evaluation on 486 minutes of real-world bus surveillance video demonstrates the potential of grounded edge-cloud reasoning for passenger-level payment analytics while highlighting the challenges posed by degraded video conditions.

AI.tldr: GHR-VLM integrates edge-grounded visual grounding with a vision-language model to enable zero-shot, passenger-centric analytics from long transit videos, using an edge-cloud loop to extract grounding clips and a two-stage VLM reasoning to classify boarding and payment behavior, with evaluation on real surveillance data.
AI.motivation: Address the gap between supervised video models requiring annotations and direct application of VLMs to long surveillance videos, by exploiting labeled grounding signals and reducing cloud inference.
AI.method: Edge component tracks door status and segments passenger clips; backend VLM operates on grounded clips; two-stage coarse-to-fine refinement of spatiotemporal evidence to identify boarding and payment behavior.
AI.result: Demonstrated on 486 minutes of real-world bus surveillance; grounded edge-cloud reasoning improves passenger-level payment analytics and reveals degradation challenges in video quality.
AI.conclusion: Grounded visual reasoning with edge-cloud architecture is promising for zero-shot transit analytics; practical viability depends on robust grounding under degraded video conditions and efficiency gains from selective VLM invocation.

title: nuTruck: Benchmarking Autonomous Driving Planning for Distributed Electric-drive Trucks
summary: The dominance of traditional rule-based methods in autonomous driving has gradually been replaced by learning-based approaches. While learning-based planners have achieved considerable success in passenger vehicles, their performance on heavy-duty trucks, particularly modern distributed electric-drive trucks (DETs), remains largely unexplored. To facilitate research and application of learning-based planners in DETs, this letter presents the first high-fidelity benchmark, called nuTruck, designed to support large-scale neural network training and closed-loop evaluation. Given the complex dynamics and high rollover susceptibility of DETs, we first incorporate a highly accurate nonlinear truck dynamical model into the simulation, which enables independent driving and steering of all wheels and captures dynamic load transfer caused by acceleration, deceleration, and cornering, thereby allowing quantitative assessment of rollover risk in closed-loop simulation. Second, we adapt several rule-based and learning-based planners as baselines for DETs and evaluate their performance in closed-loop simulation. Finally, using real-world driving scenarios from the nuPlan dataset, we conduct extensive closed-loop evaluations, analyzing not only conventional collision-free planning performance, but also the dynamical safety of the planned trajectories. The proposed nuTruck benchmark is expected to serve as a new standard for fair and realistic evaluation of autonomous driving planners on DETs.

AI.tldr: Introduces nuTruck, a high-fidelity benchmark for autonomous driving planners on heavy-duty distributed electric-drive trucks (DETs): a nonlinear truck dynamics model with independent wheel actuation and load transfer, integrated into simulation for closed-loop evaluation; adapts rule-based and learning-based planners as baselines; uses nuPlan-based real-world scenarios to assess collision-free performance and dynamical safety; aims to standardize fair, realistic evaluation for DET planning.
AI.motivation: Heavy-duty trucks present dynamics and rollover risks not adequately captured by existing baselines; lack of benchmarks for learning-based planners on DETs hinders progress; need large-scale training and realistic closed-loop evaluation.
AI.method: Develop a high-fidelity DET simulation with independent wheel steering/driving and load transfer; integrate an accurate nonlinear truck dynamic model; adapt existing planners as baselines; perform closed-loop evaluations on nuPlan-derived scenarios; analyze collision-free performance and rollover risk.
AI.result: nuTruck provides a benchmark framework enabling large-scale NN training and closed-loop evaluation; demonstrates evaluation of both conventional collision-free planning and dynamical safety; establishes a new standard for DET planning evaluation.
AI.conclusion: nuTruck is positioned as a standard benchmark for realistic, fair evaluation of DET planners, promoting adoption of learning-based methods in heavy-duty trucking.

title: From Novice to Expert: Cost-Aware Bandits for Evolving Worker Performance in Crowdsensing
comment: 14 pages, 10 figures, 3 tables, submitted for possible journal publication
summary: Mobile crowdsensing (MC) recruits mobile users to perform sensing tasks using their smartphones, enabling large-scale applications such as traffic monitoring and environmental sensing. A fundamental challenge is online worker recruitment under uncertainty, where the platform must learn workers' sensing performance while operating with a limited budget. Existing learning-based MC recruitment methods typically assume that each worker's sensing quality is stationary with a fixed mean over time. In practice, however, worker performance often improves with experience and eventually stabilizes, while the incurred sensing cost can be unknown in advance due to time-varying device and context states. In this paper, we study a budget-constrained online recruitment problem in which the platform selects one worker in each round, observes the sensing quality and incurred cost, where the expected sensing quality of each worker increases with experience and eventually converges to a plateau, and repeats until the budget is exhausted. We formulate this problem as a structured bandit model where each worker's expected reward evolves according to an unknown increasing-then-converging function of its participation count, and each worker has an unknown expected cost. We develop a cost-aware online learning framework that jointly learns evolving reward trajectories and heterogeneous costs, detects performance saturation, and allocates the limited budget to maximize long-term sensing utility. We provide theoretical performance guarantees and validate the proposed approach through extensive experiments, demonstrating consistent improvements over baselines that ignore experience-driven dynamics or assume known costs.

AI.tldr: A budgeted online recruitment framework for mobile crowdsensing that models worker performance as an unknown, increasing-then-converging function of participation with unknown costs, using a structured bandit approach to jointly learn trajectories and costs, detect saturation, and allocate budget with theoretical guarantees and empirical validation.
AI.motivation: Recruiting workers online under budget with uncertain, non-stationary performance and unknown costs is challenging. Existing methods often assume stationary rewards or known costs, which misalign with real-world device and context variability and experience gains.
AI.method: Model the problem as a structured bandit where each worker’s expected reward grows with participation count following an unknown increasing-then-converging function, and each worker has an unknown cost. Develop a cost-aware online learning framework that jointly learns evolving reward trajectories and costs, detects performance saturation, and optimally allocates the limited budget across rounds to maximize long-term sensing utility. Provide theoretical performance guarantees and validate via extensive experiments against baselines.
AI.result: The approach yields theoretical performance guarantees (e.g., regret bounds) and demonstrates empirical improvements over baselines that ignore experience-driven dynamics or assume known costs across simulated and/or real datasets.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating experience-driven dynamics and cost uncertainty into MC recruitment enables more effective budget use and improved long-term sensing utility, with provable guarantees and solid empirical validation.

title: UniPhysGen: Unified Physical Grounding for Simulation-Ready 3D Assets
summary: Physically grounded 3D assets are increasingly important for embodied AI and robotic simulation. However, most existing 3D assets lack unified physical semantics, including articulation semantics and intrinsic physical properties, required for realistic interaction. Current approaches either treat these semantics independently or rely on canonicalized object structures, limiting robustness across heterogeneous 3D assets. We present UniPhys, a scalable framework for automatically transforming raw 3D assets into simulation-ready assets with unified physical semantics. Based on UniPhys, we construct UniPhys-40K, a large-scale physically grounded dataset, together with UniPhys-Bench, a carefully verified benchmark for unified physical grounding evaluation. We further introduce UniPhysGen, a unified physical grounding model that jointly reasons over articulation semantics and intrinsic physical properties. UniPhysGen incorporates geometry-robust articulation grounding to mitigate geometric shortcut bias under heterogeneous part decompositions. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across articulation grounding and intrinsic physical property estimation tasks, while the resulting assets can be directly deployed in robotic simulation environments for realistic physical interaction. Our code and dataset will be available at https://github.com/breezexian/UniPhysGen.

AI.tldr: Proposes UniPhys: a scalable pipeline to convert raw 3D assets into simulation-ready assets with unified articulation semantics and intrinsic physical properties; introduces UniPhys-40K dataset and UniPhys-Bench benchmark; presents UniPhysGen, a model for joint articulation and physical property grounding with geometry-robust grounding; achieves state-of-the-art results and enables direct robotic simulation deployment; code and data released.
AI.motivation: To enable robust, unified physical grounding across heterogeneous 3D assets, addressing the fragmentation where articulation semantics and intrinsic physical properties are treated separately or rely on canonicalized object structures, limiting realism in embodied AI and robotics.
AI.method: 1) UniPhys framework to transform raw 3D assets into simulation-ready assets with unified semantics. 2) UniPhys-40K: large-scale physically grounded dataset. 3) UniPhys-Bench: benchmark for unified physical grounding evaluation. 4) UniPhysGen: a unified physical grounding model that jointly reasons about articulation semantics and intrinsic physical properties, including geometry-robust articulation grounding to reduce geometric shortcut bias from varied part decompositions.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show state-of-the-art performance on articulation grounding and intrinsic physical property estimation. The resulting assets can be directly deployed in robotic simulation environments for realistic interaction.
AI.conclusion: The UniPhys framework, dataset, and model provide a scalable, robust solution for unified physical grounding of 3D assets, enabling realistic interaction in embodied AI and robotics; code and dataset will be available to the community.

title: The Nonsmooth Impact Direction (NSID) of Robotic Systems
summary: Collisions of rigid-link robots and rigid environments are often modeled as instantaneous events. Under this idealization, the impact forces become impulsive and the system velocities nonsmooth. In this work, we systematically analyze pre- and post-impact velocities focusing on what we refer to as the nonsmooth impact direction (NSID). We show that it is a characteristic direction of a robotic impact and largely independent of contact properties. The results are directly applicable to large classes of backdrivable robotic systems with rigid links. We address particularities of systems with nonelastic and flexible joints, unconstrained as well as constrained systems. Further, we show that the approach direction w.r.t the NSID sets the direction of the impulsive force in frictional, inelastic impacts. The comprehensive theoretical analysis of this work supported by an experimental validation may serve as a foundation for future planning and control algorithms for various robotic impact applications. These can include humanoid locomotion on a slippery surface or repetitive hammering.

AI.tldr: Introduces and analyzes the nonsmooth impact direction (NSID) for rigid-link robot impacts, showing NSID as a principal, contact-property–independent impulse direction with implications for planning/control; validated experimentally.
AI.motivation: Provide a rigorous understanding of impact direction in robotic collisions to improve planning and control under impulsive forces.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis of pre- and post-impact velocities to identify NSID across systems (backdrivable rigid-link robots, nonelastic/flexible joints, constrained and unconstrained). Includes exploration of how the NSID governs impulsive force direction in frictional, inelastic impacts and supports experimental validation.
AI.result: NSID is a characteristic direction largely independent of contact properties. The approach direction relative to the NSID determines the impulsive force direction in frictional, inelastic impacts. The framework applies to a broad class of robotic systems and is supported by experimental validation.
AI.conclusion: Provides a foundational framework for planning and control algorithms in robotic impact tasks (e.g., humanoid locomotion on slick surfaces, repetitive hammering), accommodating various joint types and constraint conditions.

title: Structured Reinforcement Learning for Bayesian Persuasion : Application to Intelligent Interactive Driving
summary: Interactive driving, wherein an intelligent lead vehicle equipped with real-time traffic data coordinates route choices of connected vehicles, offers a promising approach to dynamic traffic management. To address the challenge of harmonising decisions, this paper considers the strategic information revealing framework of Bayesian persuasion. Here, the principal (lead vehicle) aims to guide the agent's (connected vehicle) partially observable sequential decision making towards its own objectives by selectively revealing information, such as real-time traffic ahead, using signals. However, the agent's farsighted response to maximize its long-term reward, renders the principal's signaling strategy design computationally challenging. We propose an online structured reinforcement learning framework to synthesize computationally efficient signaling strategy which is persuasive for a far-sighted agent. The main contributions of the paper are as follows: (i) For a monotonic agent with approximate best response, we propose MAPL, a structured policy learning algorithm for faster online learning, (ii) Identification of sufficient conditions for the supermodular structure of the Q function of the principal for a monotonic agent, (iii) Identification of sufficient conditions to ensure the persuasiveness of the principal's signaling strategy, (iv) Supermodular Q learning for Principal (SQP), which leverages the supermodular structure of principal's action value to synthesize computationally efficient signaling strategy that is persuasive for a monotonic learning agent, (v) Numerical analysis considering a real-time application of Bayesian persuasive driving for lane selection demonstrates that the proposed method is 30% cost efficient for optimising travelling rewards of both the lead and connected vehicle compared to the existing methodologies for signaling strategy design.

AI.tldr: A structured reinforcement-learning framework for Bayesian persuasion in interactive driving, introducing MAPL and SQP to craft persuasive signaling for farsighted agents and demonstrating ~30% efficiency gains in lane selection.
AI.motivation: To manage dynamic traffic by letting a lead vehicle strategically reveal information to influence partially observable, sequential decisions of connected vehicles, addressing computational challenges from farsighted agents.
AI.method: Online structured reinforcement learning framework for monotonic agents with approximate best responses. Develop MAPL (structured policy learning) for faster learning, identify conditions for supermodular Q-function of the principal, specify persuasiveness conditions, propose SQP (Supermodular Q-learning for Principal) to exploit the supermodular structure, and validate with a real-time Bayesian persuasive driving scenario for lane selection.
AI.result: MAPL enables faster online learning; identified sufficient conditions for supermodular Q-functions and persuasiveness; SQP leverages supermodularity to efficiently compute persuasive signaling; real-time lane-selection case shows ~30% improvement in travelling rewards for lead and connected vehicles compared to existing signaling strategies.
AI.conclusion: The framework mitigates computational complexity in designing persuasive signals for farsighted agents, yielding efficient, persuasive signaling policies with tangible performance gains in dynamic driving applications.

title: OvisOCR2 Technical Report
summary: We introduce OvisOCR2, a 0.8B document parsing model. OvisOCR2 is designed as an end-to-end parser: given a document page image, it generates a Markdown representation in natural reading order, covering text, formulas, tables, and visual regions. We build a data engine that combines filtered real-document annotations with synthetic pages whose rendered images and Markdown targets are derived from the same HTML source. The training recipe includes supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning on a 4B branch with a multi-component reward design, on-policy distillation into the 0.8B model, and model fusion. On OmniDocBench v1.6, OvisOCR2 achieves a state-of-the-art overall score of 96.58, placing an end-to-end model at the top of this leaderboard previously dominated by pipeline methods and highlighting the potential of end-to-end document parsing. On PureDocBench, OvisOCR2 also achieves the highest Avg3 score of 75.06. Beyond these two public benchmarks, we evaluate OvisOCR2 on an in-house benchmark designed to cover a broader set of long-tail and challenging scenarios. OvisOCR2 obtains the best overall performance among the compared methods, providing further evidence of its generalization and robustness. OvisOCR2 is available at https://huggingface.co/ATH-MaaS/OvisOCR2.

AI.tldr: 0.8B end-to-end document parser (OvisOCR2) produces Markdown from page images and achieves SOTA results on OmniDocBench v1.6 and PureDocBench, with strong generalization; available on HuggingFace.
AI.motivation: Advance from pipeline-centric document parsing to an end-to-end model that jointly parses text, formulas, tables, and visual regions with robust performance.
AI.method: Data engine combining filtered real annotations with synthetic pages derived from HTML sources. Training includes supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning on a 4B-parameter branch with a multi-component reward, on-policy distillation into the 0.8B model, and model fusion.
AI.result: On OmniDocBench v1.6: overall score 96.58, top end-to-end model; on PureDocBench: Avg3 75.06; strong generalization evidenced by competitive in-house benchmark.
AI.conclusion: End-to-end document parsing is viable and beneficial; OvisOCR2 demonstrates strong performance and generalization; model is publicly available.

title: Dynamical Vehicle Orienteering Problem for Multi-Rotor Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
comment: 28 pages, 10 figures, preprint submitted to European Journal of Operational Research
summary: This paper introduces the Dynamical Vehicle Orienteering Problem (DVOP), a generalization of the Orienteering Problem (OP). The OP maximizes the reward collected from spatial targets under a limited travel budget; the DVOP extends it by accounting for both external and vehicle-actuated forces. We study the DVOP in the context of multi-rotor Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) flight planning, using a three-dimensional Point-Mass Model (PMM) constrained by maximum velocity and acceleration magnitudes and subject to gravitational acceleration, with the travel budget expressed as a maximum flight time. Because the DVOP couples reward maximization with time-optimal trajectory planning, it cannot be formulated as a simple graph problem and solved exactly without relaxing or under-actuating the vehicle dynamics. We therefore propose two solution approaches: a Branch-and-Bound (BnB) procedure that combines Non-Linear Programming (NLP) and Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) to provide high-quality solutions, and a Large Neighborhood Search (LNS) metaheuristic that supplies an initial reward bound and scales to instances intractable for the BnB. The BnB relies on a novel MILP formulation of travel costs based on minimum-time trajectory primitives through target triplets, yielding a tight reward upper bound, while the LNS uses limited thrust decomposition to compute fast, high-quality PMM trajectories. Experiments on benchmark instances show improvements of up to 37 % over state-of-the-art solutions for the Kinematic Orienteering Problem, and a real-world deployment on a multi-rotor UAV verifies the proposed PMM solution trajectories.

AI.tldr: DVOP generalizes OP by integrating 3D PMM dynamics into UAV routing; proposes BnB (NLP+MILP) and LNS, achieving up to 37% improvement and real UAV validation.
AI.motivation: Need to couple reward collection with time-optimal trajectories under dynamic constraints; standard OP lacks dynamics and energy considerations.
AI.method: Model: 3D PMM with max velocity/acceleration and gravity; budget as max flight time. Solve with Branch-and-Bound using MILP for travel costs via minimum-time trajectory primitives; and Large Neighborhood Search with limited thrust decomposition to generate PMM trajectories.
AI.result: Benchmarks show up to 37% improvements over Kinematic OP; real-world multi-rotor UAV deployment confirms trajectory feasibility.
AI.conclusion: Hybrid optimization provides high-quality and scalable solutions for DVOP; integrating dynamics into OP yields better planning under time budgets.

title: Gauge-Invariant, Parameter-Insensitive Regularization for Potential Recovery from Flow on Directed Graphs
summary: Recovering a latent potential from observed flow on a directed graph (a discrete Poisson problem with Dirichlet boundaries) is ill-posed, and the standard fix backfires: ridge regularization shrinks toward a gauge-meaningless origin, collapsing and reversing the recovered ordering ($+0.81\to-0.42$ rank correlation against a planted ground truth). The gauge-invariant graph Dirichlet energy removes the hazard and delivers parameter-insensitivity: the estimate is stable across four orders of magnitude in $λ$, whereas ridge inverts the ordering for every $λ>0$. We prove the reduced solve is SPD and preserves dynamic range exactly where ridge collapses it, and localize absorbing boundaries from flow alone via a Poisson residual. The $H^1$ seminorm is classical; what is new is the gauge diagnosis, the parameter-insensitivity it buys, and an ablation showing the result is robust to the extraction method. On three public clickstream corpora the gauge-invariant estimate retains $28$--$41\%$ of the interior dynamic range while ridge collapses to as little as $0.2\%$. The same gauge invariance carries into graph neural networks -- neutralizing the constant mode per layer prevents the oversmoothing that collapses a deep directed GCN -- linking this classical inverse problem to a central question in graph learning.

AI.tldr: Gauge-invariant Dirichlet energy yields parameter-insensitive, stable recovery of latent potentials on directed graphs, overcoming ridge-induced collapse and preserving dynamic range; extends to directed GCN by removing constant modes.
AI.motivation: Inverse problem for latent potential from observed directed flow is ill-posed; standard ridge regularization introduces gauge ambiguity and collapses interior dynamic range; need a gauge-invariant formulation with stable behavior across regularization strength.
AI.method: Introduce gauge-invariant graph Dirichlet energy; derive reduced SPD solve; show gauge-invariant energy yields correct dynamic range; localize absorbing boundaries with Poisson residual; perform ablation; apply to three clickstream datasets; extend to graph neural networks by removing constant-mode across layers.
AI.result: Estimator stable across four orders of magnitude in λ; preserves dynamic range (28–41% of interior) vs ridge collapsing to ~0.2%; reduced solve is SPD and preserves dynamic range; can localize absorbing boundaries; gauge invariance persists in directed GCNs preventing oversmoothing.
AI.conclusion: Gauge diagnosis yields parameter-insensitive, robust inversion for directed Poisson problems; the approach connects classical inverse problems with core questions in graph learning and GNN design by managing gauge/constant modes.

title: Human4K: A Large-Scale 4K Multi-View Mocap Dataset for Whole-Body 3D Human Reconstruction
summary: Recent advances in 3D human reconstruction have improved overall performance, yet current models still fail in the most challenging real-world scenarios. They often produce unstable geometry, inaccurate limb articulation and unreliable predictions under depth ambiguity or self-occlusion. A key reason is that existing datasets still lack the combination of high-resolution images, high-precision annotations and diverse whole-body motions required to support robust reconstruction. To address this gap, we present Human4K, a large-scale 4K multi-view whole-body human reconstruction dataset with mocap-accurate SMPL-X annotations. Human4K contains over six million 4K images captured by an eight-view high-resolution camera system synchronized with a professional Vicon motion capture setup, covering 11 subjects performing complex, highly articulated and strongly self-occluded full-body motions. All sequences are processed by a Motion-Retargeting and Refinement Module (MRRM) to ensure precise alignment for the full body and extremities. Experimental results show that training with Human4K consistently improves whole-body reconstruction on standard benchmarks, with particularly large gains for hands, feet and depth-ambiguous limb configurations.

AI.tldr: A large-scale 4K multi-view whole-body reconstruction dataset (Human4K) with mocap-accurate SMPL-X annotations and a Motion-Retargeting/Refinement Module (MRRM), shown to improve whole-body reconstruction, especially hands/feet under depth ambiguity.
AI.motivation: Address the lack of high-resolution, precisely annotated, diverse full-body motion data for robust 3D reconstruction; existing datasets fail under depth ambiguity, self-occlusion, and challenging motions.
AI.method: Data collection using eight-view high-resolution cameras synchronized with Vicon mocap to capture six million 4K images across 11 subjects performing complex, highly articulated motions. Processing with a Motion-Retargeting and Refinement Module (MRRM) to ensure precise alignment of the full body and extremities, and providing mocap-accurate SMPL-X annotations.
AI.result: Training with Human4K yields consistent improvements on standard whole-body reconstruction benchmarks, with particularly large gains for hands, feet, and depth-ambiguous limb configurations.
AI.conclusion: Human4K and the MRRM pipeline advance robust whole-body reconstruction by providing high-quality, diverse data with precise annotations, enabling better generalization to challenging real-world scenarios.

title: Vision-Based Obstacle Separation for Strawberry Harvesting in Clusters Using Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
summary: Selective harvesting in clustered strawberry environments is challenging because ripe fruits are often occluded by surrounding unripe fruits, making direct grasping unreliable. To address this problem, this paper proposes a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework, termed VGPA, which integrates a vision-guided decision mechanism and a Progressive Adaptive Exploration Strategy (PAES) for vision-based obstacle separation and harvesting. The task was decomposed into two sequential stages: obstacle separation and target grasping. At the high level, the vision-guided mechanism improved option selection and accelerated policy convergence. At the low level, PAES improved exploration efficiency and training stability during continuous control learning. In simulation experiments, the learned policy achieved a success rate of 96.7%. In addition, sim-to-real transfer experiments on a self-developed parallel robot showed that the proposed method achieved success rates ranging from 71.7% to 88.3%, outperforming direct picking while requiring only 1.22~s more average harvesting time. These results verified the effectiveness, generalization ability, and practical potential of the proposed method for robotic harvesting in complex clustered environments.

AI.tldr: A hierarchical RL framework (VGPA) for vision-guided obstacle separation and harvesting in clustered strawberries, with a two-stage structure (obstacle separation then target grasping) and a Progressive Adaptive Exploration Strategy (PAES). Achieves 96.7% success in simulation and 71.7–88.3% sim-to-real on a parallel robot, modestly slower by ~1.22 s than direct picking.
AI.motivation: Address selective harvesting where occluded ripe fruit hinders direct grasping by integrating vision-guided decision making with an exploration-efficient learning strategy to improve policy convergence and training stability.
AI.method: Two-stage hierarchical RL: high-level vision-guided mechanism for option selection; low-level Progressive Adaptive Exploration Strategy (PAES) for exploration in continuous control. Tasks: obstacle separation followed by target grasping; sim-to-real transfer using a custom parallel robotic platform.
AI.result: Simulation success rate: 96.7%. Sim-to-real success: 71.7% to 88.3% depending on scenario. Outperforms direct picking; harvesting time increased by 1.22 seconds on average.
AI.conclusion: The VGPA framework is effective, generalizes to at least the tested sim-to-real setup, and shows practical potential for robotic harvesting in complex clustered environments.

title: The SIGReg Objective as Variational Free Energy: A Theoretical Active-Inference Account of JEPA World Models
comment: Theoretical paper; empirical validation of the stated predictions is left to separate work. 28 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables
summary: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) are the dominant design for latent world models, yet they are usually justified by empirical performance rather than a normative principle. We show that the choice of anti-collapse regulariser determines whether a JEPA's training objective, a prediction loss plus a weighted embedding regulariser, is a valid Active Inference (AIF) variational free energy. We organise four non-contrastive regularisers (VICReg, LogDet, PairDist, and SIGReg) into an entropy-estimator hierarchy indexed by a prior-miscalibration gap, and show that the gap's sign, whether the estimator bounds the latent entropy from above or below, decides whether the AIF surprise bound survives: VICReg and LogDet are unsafe upper bounds, PairDist a safe lower bound, and SIGReg eliminates the gap. We then prove a correspondence theorem: under the standard constant-noise encoder model and successful SIGReg enforcement (isotropic-Gaussian embeddings), the gap vanishes, the objective becomes an exact information bottleneck, the surprise bound is preserved, and the latent goal cost becomes an exact proxy for AIF pragmatic value, whereas VICReg leaves an irreducible second-order anisotropy term. We extend the correspondence to multi-step expected free energy, ensemble epistemic value, and a learned-policy regime, and we identify the one AIF term no current JEPA world model computes: the state-epistemic value, a future-state coverage signal. The predictions differ in kind, not degree, and are stated here as theoretical consequences left for empirical test in separate work; full proofs are in Appendix A, and the algebraic core of every result is machine-verified in Lean 4 (Appendix D).

AI.tldr: The paper shows that the anti-collapse regulariser used in Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) determines whether the training objective aligns with Active Inference variational free energy. Four non-contrastive regularisers (VICReg, LogDet, PairDist, SIGReg) form an entropy-estimator hierarchy based on a prior-miscalibration gap; VICReg/LogDet are unsafe upper bounds, PairDist is a safe lower bound, SIGReg eliminates the gap. Under constant-noise encoders and successful SIGReg (isotropic-Gaussian embeddings), the gap vanishes and the objective becomes an exact information bottleneck, preserving the surprise bound and making the latent-goal cost an exact proxy for AIF pragmatic value; VICReg retains a second-order anisotropy term. The work extends to multi-step free energy, ensemble value, and learned-policy regimes, but identifies a remaining unknown term: the state-epistemic value. Full proofs are in Appendix A, with algebraic core machine-verified in Lean 4 (Appendix D).
AI.motivation: To provide a normative, principled understanding of regularisation in JEPA-based latent world models by connecting the training objective to Active Inference free energy, and to classify anti-collapse regularisers by their impact on bounds and information bottleneck properties.
AI.method: Organize four non-contrastive regularisers (VICReg, LogDet, PairDist, SIGReg) into an entropy-estimator hierarchy via a prior-miscalibration gap; derive a correspondence theorem under a constant-noise encoder and SIGReg enforcement; prove gap behavior (sign determines upper/lower bound status) and specialize to isotropic-Gaussian embeddings; extend analysis to multi-step expected free energy, ensemble epistemic value, and learned-policy regimes; identify missing AIF term (state-epistemic value); provide full proofs in Appendix A and machine-verified core in Lean 4 (Appendix D).
AI.result: Classification of regularisers by bounds: VICReg/LogDet yield unsafe upper bounds, PairDist yields a safe lower bound, SIGReg eliminates the gap; with SIGReg and isotropic Gaussian embeddings the gap vanishes, making the objective an exact information bottleneck and preserving the surprise bound; latent-goal cost becomes an exact proxy for AIF pragmatic value; VICReg retains an irreducible second-order anisotropy term; extended results cover multi-step and policy-regimes; identifies the uncomputed state-epistemic value as a missing term; empirical validation left for separate work; proofs in Appendix A; Lean 4 verification in Appendix D.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a normative criterion for JEPA regularisation aligned with Active Inference, showing that the choice of anti-collapse regulariser crucially determines whether the JEPA objective constitutes a valid AIF free energy, with SIGReg under isotropic assumptions yielding exact equivalence; highlights an open term (state-epistemic value) and motivates empirical testing to validate predicted distinctions between regularisers.

title: Beyond Color Geometry: Evaluating Human-Like Color Representations in Vision Models
comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables submitted to 2026 Joint 14th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 27th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS 2026)
summary: Do vision models see colors the way humans do? Existing evaluations of color representations usually compare them with geometric spaces such as CIELAB or with discrete color labels. These references capture perceptual distance or category membership, but not the graded way in which people organize colors. We evaluate color grounding against a fuzzy perceptual model with 86 graded categories fitted to human survey data. The framework can be applied to any image encoder and measures three complementary properties: category boundaries, category compactness, and graded alignment beyond what color geometry alone can explain. Across eleven Vision Transformer encoders, the category-level results are broadly similar, whereas graded alignment differs substantially. Masked Autoencoders achieve the strongest beyond-geometry alignment, with confidence intervals that do not overlap those of the other encoders. A layer-wise analysis further shows that masked reconstruction preserves this structure toward the output. On natural images, MAE represents surface color globally, while language-supervised models encode color more strongly in relation to the foreground object. These results show that human-like color grounding has several distinct aspects that should not be reduced to a single score.

AI.tldr: Evaluates color grounding in 11 Vision Transformer encoders using a fuzzy 86-category perceptual model, highlighting that color understanding has multiple facets beyond geometry, with Masked Autoencoders (MAE) showing strongest alignment to human color semantics.
AI.motivation: Current color representations are evaluated against geometry (e.g., CIELAB) or discrete labels, but these do not capture the graded, human-like organization of colors. The study aims to quantify multiple facets of color grounding—category boundaries, category compactness, and graded alignment—against human data.
AI.method: Apply a fuzzy perceptual model with 86 graded categories fitted to human survey data to any image encoder. Compute three metrics (category boundaries, category compactness, graded alignment). Evaluate 11 ViT encoders, including MAE and various language-supervised models. Perform layer-wise analyses and test on natural images to distinguish global surface color from object-related color.
AI.result: Category-level results are broadly similar across encoders, but graded alignment varies. MAE achieves the strongest beyond-geometry (graded) alignment, with non-overlapping confidence intervals compared to other encoders. Layer-wise analysis shows masked reconstruction preserves this structure toward output. On natural images, MAE encodes surface color globally, while language-supervised models encode color more in relation to the foreground object.
AI.conclusion: Human-like color grounding comprises multiple distinct aspects that cannot be captured by a single score. Different training objectives yield different color-grounding properties, and MAE's reconstruction objective particularly supports graded alignment with human data.

title: A Deployed Hybrid Vehicle-in-the-Loop Platform for Validating Cooperative Perception
comment: 4 pages, 5 figures, to be presented in the IEEE ITSC 2026 Industry Track
summary: European safety regulation now permits a large share of automated-driving homologation evidence to be produced virtually, provided a validated physical-virtual facility generates it. We present a deployed hybrid Vehicle-in-the-Loop (ViL) platform that couples a real instrumented vehicle with a CARLA-based digital twin (DT) through a V2X message pipeline, and we report its first integrated operation on a public-road-representative test track. A real vehicle streams ETSI-compliant CAM/CPM messages into the DT, where a GPU-accelerated Cooperative Perception (CP) module fuses them into a probabilistic occupancy grid during scenario runtime. We demonstrate the platform on a multi-vehicle double T-intersection scenario, characterise the CP workload across nominal, rain and night conditions and five localization-noise levels, and discuss the platform's current architectural limits and the engineering targets they define. The results show that CP substantially widens field-of-view (FoV) coverage and improves occupied-cell recall, and that beyond a moderate localization-noise threshold, positioning uncertainty, and not weather, becomes the dominant error source. We outline the platform's trajectory toward a Mediterranean operational design domain (ODD) testing service.

AI.tldr: A deployed hybrid Vehicle-in-the-Loop (ViL) platform couples a real instrumented vehicle with a CARLA-based digital twin for virtual homologation work; first public-road-representative demonstration with CP fused occupancy grid; CP improves FoV and recall; localization noise becomes the dominant error source beyond moderate levels; outlines trajectory toward a Mediterranean ODD testing service.
AI.motivation: Regulatory shift permitting virtual homologation with validated physical-virtual facilities; need an integrated ViL workflow and cooperative perception on realistic test tracks to support regulatory acceptance and establishment of an ODD-specific testing service.
AI.method: Real vehicle streams ETSI CAM/CPM messages into a CARLA-based DT via a V2X pipeline; GPU-accelerated Cooperative Perception (CP) module fuses messages into a probabilistic occupancy grid during runtime; demonstration on a multi-vehicle double T-intersection; evaluation across nominal, rain, night conditions and five localization-noise levels; analysis of CP workload and architectural limits.
AI.result: CP substantially widens field-of-view and improves occupied-cell recall; beyond a moderate localization-noise threshold, positioning uncertainty becomes the dominant error source over weather; first integrated ViL operation on a public-road-representative test track; defines steps toward a Mediterranean operational design domain (ODD) testing service.
AI.conclusion: The ViL platform demonstrates feasibility of virtual homologation with physical testing integration; cooperative perception yields tangible coverage and accuracy gains; localization accuracy emerges as a key bottleneck; paper outlines concrete engineering targets and a path toward an ODD-based testing service.

title: FastCentNN: Accelerating Centroid Neural Network with Entropy Proxy
summary: Centroid neural network (CentNN) is an unsupervised competitive learning algorithm in which centroid splitting is triggered only after strict local stabilization, often leading to prolonged low-movement training phases before model expansion. This report proposes FastCentNN, an accelerated variant that addresses this inefficiency by introducing an early splitting strategy based on the total centroid movement per epoch, which serves as a training entropy proxy. As a result, FastCentNN reduces unnecessary reassignment epochs while preserving the original winner-loser learning dynamics. FastCentNN supports both absolute and stage-relative movement thresholds, allowing the splitting criterion to remain either fixed or adaptive throughout training. Experiments on some benchmark datasets show that FastCentNN consistently achieves clustering quality comparable to CentNN while reducing runtime by up to 16% on synthetic 2D datasets and about 5% on high-dimensional datasets. FastCentNN therefore provides a practical and efficient drop-in replacement for CentNN, retaining its online adaptive learning behavior while offering a simple and interpretable speed-stability trade-off through configurable splitting thresholds.

AI.tldr: FastCentNN is an accelerated variant of CentNN that enables early centroid splitting based on total centroid movement per epoch, acting as a training entropy proxy. It preserves winner-loser dynamics while reducing unnecessary reassignment epochs.
AI.motivation: Address inefficiency in CentNN where splitting is delayed until strict local stabilization, causing prolonged low-movement phases and slow training.
AI.method: Introduce an early splitting criterion using the total centroid movement per epoch; support absolute and stage-relative movement thresholds; allow fixed or adaptive thresholds; maintain winner-loser learning dynamics; evaluate on benchmark datasets.
AI.result: Clustering quality remains comparable to CentNN; runtime reduced by up to 16% on synthetic 2D datasets and ~5% on high-dimensional datasets.
AI.conclusion: FastCentNN offers a practical drop-in replacement for CentNN, delivering a simple, interpretable speed-stability trade-off through configurable splitting thresholds while preserving online adaptive learning.

title: From Surface Forecasting to Observability Forecasting: A Latent World Model for Cloud-Aware EO Monitoring
summary: The bottleneck of Earth Observation processing chains is not the arrival of new imagery but whether the surface is actually visible when the image arrives. We study this as an observability forecasting problem on EarthNet2021. Given recent multispectral imagery and exogenous weather drivers, the goal is to predict whether the next acquisition will be usable and, if not, when a usable view is likely to return. To do this, we adapt LeWorldModel, a joint-embedding predictive architecture world model, to cloud-aware Earth Observation sequences. The final pipeline converts raw minicubes into episodic HDF5 sequences with five image channels (blue, green, red, near-infrared, cloud mask) and eight meteorological and calendar covariates. The resulting model has 18.0M trainable parameters and is trained from scratch on 23,904 training episodes. The trained leWorldModel is evaluated under a locked protocol: linear probes are fit on train only, calibration choices are set on an internal validation split, and the fitted heads are then frozen for valsplit, IID, OOD, and extreme evaluation. On the full frozen-bundle observability benchmark, LeWorldModel consistently outperforms persistence. For next-step usability, balanced accuracy ranges from 0.769 to 0.887, compared with 0.493 to 0.556 for persistence. For exact first-usable-horizon prediction, accuracy ranges from 0.602 to 0.806, compared with 0.120 to 0.369 for persistence. Against a frozen LightGBM baseline fit on the same training windows, LeWorldModel is better on continuous clear/cloud regression and on exact recovery timing on valsplit, IID, and extreme, while LightGBM is stronger on the simpler binary any-usable-within-six task and is more robust on OOD. In separate sampled diagnostic analyses, LeWM also produces strong ranking-based anomaly signals under synthetic temporal inconsistencies.

AI.tldr: LeWorldModel improves Earth Observation observability forecasting by predicting whether the next acquisition will be usable, outperforming persistence and a frozen LightGBM baseline across next-step usability and exact first-usable-horizon timing; it also yields sensitive anomaly signals.
AI.motivation: The main bottleneck in EO processing is visibility, not image arrival. Predicting if the next image will be usable (given recent multispectral imagery and weather covariates) enables proactive task planning and data fusion. The work applies a world-model approach to cloud-aware EO sequences on EarthNet2021.
AI.method: Adapt LeWorldModel (joint-embedding predictive world model) to cloud-aware EO sequences. Raw minicubes are converted to episodic HDF5 sequences with five image channels (blue, green, red, NIR, cloud mask) and eight meteorological/calendar covariates. The model has 18.0M parameters, trained from scratch on 23,904 training episodes. Evaluation uses a locked protocol with train-only linear probes, internal-validation calibration, and frozen heads evaluated on valsplit, IID, OOD, and extreme settings.
AI.result: LeWorldModel consistently outperforms persistence on the full frozen-bundle observability benchmark. Balanced accuracy ranges 0.769–0.887 vs 0.493–0.556 for persistence. Exact first-usable-horizon accuracy 0.602–0.806 vs 0.120–0.369 for persistence. Against a frozen LightGBM baseline trained on the same windows, LeWorldModel improves continuous clear/cloud regression and exact recovery timing on valsplit/IID/extreme, while LightGBM performs better on the simpler binary task of any-usable-within-six and is more robust on OOD. Separate analyses reveal strong ranking-based anomaly signals under synthetic temporal inconsistencies.
AI.conclusion: A scalable, model-based EO observability forecaster that surpasses strong baselines and yields useful anomaly signals, offering actionable predictions for when usable imagery will reappear and enabling more robust data planning under cloud cover.

title: Learning Robust Execution in Robotic Manipulation with Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: Robotic manipulation poses fundamental challenges due to uncertainty, long-horizon execution, and compounding errors, which can easily destabilize execution and lead to task failure. Although recent vision-language-action (VLA) models exhibit strong generalization, they typically lack explicit mechanisms to assess execution stability and to recover when execution deviates from its nominal behavior. In this paper, we propose: (1) two complementary metrics to assess execution quality at runtime, and (2) an agentic reinforcement learning framework that learns to restore effective execution through high-level decision-making rather than directly learning low-level actions. In this framework, an agentic policy reasons over recent execution history and selects among a small set of execution modes to regulate the execution process. Under execution degradation, it triggers appropriate recovery mechanisms to restore the robot to previously visited nominal states, enabling the task to continue. We evaluate the proposed method on the LIBERO benchmark, achieving up to a 13.7% improvement in success rate under standard settings and up to a 39.2% improvement under disturbance settings, demonstrating substantially enhanced execution robustness.

AI.tldr: Introduces runtime execution-quality metrics and an agentic RL framework that uses high-level mode selection to recover robust robotic manipulation under uncertainty, improving LIBERO performance.
AI.motivation: Robotic manipulation suffers from uncertainty, long-horizon execution, and compounding errors. Vision-language-action models lack explicit mechanisms to assess runtime stability and to recover from deviations, limiting robustness.
AI.method: Proposes two complementary runtime metrics to assess execution quality, and an agentic policy that reasons over recent execution history to choose among a small set of execution modes, triggering recovery to return to previously visited nominal states when degraded.
AI.result: Demonstrates improved robustness on LIBERO, with up to 13.7% higher success rate under standard settings and up to 39.2% under disturbance settings.
AI.conclusion: High-level agentic control over execution modes and recovery mechanisms can significantly enhance robustness of VLA-based manipulation without learning low-level actions.

title: How the Hessian-Spectrum of Neural Networks Depends on Data
summary: The Hessian matrix is an important quantity of interest when it comes to studying the loss landscape and optimization dynamics in deep learning, as well as designing measures of generalization, second-order learning algorithms, etc. Prior works have focused on empirical results or pursued a theoretical treatment under overly simplified settings. In this work, we derive the eigenvalues of the Hessian of linear networks with arbitrary widths and depths, and datasets with an arbitrary number of samples, features, and labels. Importantly, for classification tasks with MSE loss, we identify that the sharpness of the solution is directly related to the maximum proportion of samples belonging to any class. We empirically validate our predictions and systematically analyze the effects of shedding the impractical assumptions one at a time, as well as incorporating nonlinearities. We observe that our predictions are considerably robust in most cases, allowing us to extend our conclusions to more practical learning setups.

AI.tldr: Analytical derivation of Hessian eigenvalues for linear networks of arbitrary width/depth and datasets; for classification with MSE loss, sharpness relates to the largest class proportion; empirical validation and robustness as assumptions are relaxed, including nonlinearity.
AI.motivation: Hessian spectrum encodes loss landscape and generalization; prior work either empirical or under simplified assumptions; derive exact spectrum for general linear networks to understand sharpness/optimization dynamics.
AI.method: Derive the Hessian eigenvalues analytically for linear networks with arbitrary widths/depths and datasets with arbitrary samples, features, labels; specialize to classification with MSE loss; characterize sharpness via class proportion; perform empirical validation and ablations including nonlinearity.
AI.result: Analytical Hessian spectrum obtained; sharpness tied to maximum class proportion under MSE for classification; empirical validation supports predictions; predictions robust as impractical assumptions are removed and nonlinearity is introduced.
AI.conclusion: Provides a general analytical framework for Hessian spectra in broad linear-network settings; links sharpness to dataset class distribution; demonstrates robustness and applicability to more realistic learning setups.

title: Exploratory, Communicative, and Deployable: Vision-Driven Embodied Agents for Open-World Mobile Manipulation
comment: Accepted to ECCV 2026. 57 pages. Code available at https://github.com/InternRobotics/REAL
summary:
Real-world deployment of embodied agents requires active exploration, visual grounding, and interactive intent disambiguation. However, existing frameworks often rely on privileged simulator states or assume complete instructions, bypassing realistic deployment challenges. To bridge this gap, we present REAL, an agentic framework for open-world mobile manipulation. REAL establishes sim-to-real-consistent environment APIs without oracle perception and integrates a simulated user to enable human-in-the-loop interaction. Within this environment, we design diverse task compositions to drive data collection, supervised fine-tuning, and online reinforcement learning, systematically optimizing agent performance. To comprehensively evaluate this approach, we introduce REAL-Bench, a benchmark spanning 241 tasks across active exploration, visual distraction, articulated manipulation, and interactive disambiguation.
  Experimental results demonstrate that our trained agent outperforms leading commercial closed-source VLMs on interactive tasks with a 56.9% success rate. Further empirical analysis reveals that our hierarchical training pipeline successfully aligns the model's tool-use capabilities while maintaining robust open-vocabulary reasoning under extended exploration horizons. Finally, we deploy and evaluate our framework on a physical dual-arm mobile robot, where it achieves a 78.3% end-to-end success rate over 60 real-world episodes. These physical trials demonstrate robust zero-shot transferability to unseen household scenarios, validating that our sim-to-real-consistent design successfully bridges the reality gap for long-horizon mobile manipulation. Code is available at https://github.com/InternRobotics/REAL.

AI.tldr: REAL is a sim-to-real-consistent framework for open-world mobile manipulation that integrates a simulated user for human-in-the-loop interaction, enabling data collection, supervised fine-tuning, and online RL via diverse task compositions. It introduces REAL-Bench (241 tasks) and demonstrates strong real-world performance, including zero-shot transfer to unseen homes and robust tool-use with open-vocabulary reasoning.
AI.motivation: Bridging the gap between simulated training and real-world deployment of embodied agents. Current frameworks rely on privileged simulator states or assume complete instructions, limiting active exploration, visual grounding, and interactive intent disambiguation in real settings.
AI.method: Develop REAL with sim-to-real-consistent environment APIs lacking oracle perception and a simulated user for human-in-the-loop interaction. Use diverse task compositions to drive data collection, supervised fine-tuning, and online reinforcement learning. Evaluate via REAL-Bench (241 tasks across exploration, distraction, manipulation, disambiguation) and deploy on a physical dual-arm mobile robot.
AI.result: Agent outperforms leading commercial closed-source VLMs on interactive tasks with a 56.9% success rate. Hierarchical training aligns tool-use with robust open-vocabulary reasoning under long horizons. On a real dual-arm mobile robot, achieves 78.3% end-to-end success over 60 episodes with strong zero-shot transfer to unseen households.
AI.conclusion: A sim-to-real-consistent design coupled with human-in-the-loop interaction and hierarchical training effectively bridges the reality gap for long-horizon mobile manipulation, delivering robust open-vocabulary reasoning and real-world transfer. Code is available online.

title: Recursive ArUco Markers: A Scalable Fiducial Marker Design for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Landing Pads
summary: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) increasingly rely on visual fiducial markers for autonomous navigation and precision landing. However, standard markers suffer from limited operational ranges, becoming undetectable when the camera is either too far or too close. While recursive and fractal markers have been proposed to address this issue, existing approaches either require the marker's center to remain visible, making them vulnerable to occlusion, or are limited in their recursion depth and placement. We propose a novel Recursive ArUco marker design. Our method allows any standard fiducial marker to be transformed into a recursive marker with an arbitrary depth. By employing a modified bit-sampling strategy during detection, we embed complete markers within both the black and white bits of the parent marker. This approach guarantees unlimited recursion depth and robust detection even with partial occlusion, as it does not rely on the marker's center being visible. Furthermore, by maintaining a single, unique identifier across all recursive scales, our proposal provides an extensive dictionary of multiple unique landing pads. This capability allows fleets of UAVs to operate simultaneously, with each drone landing at its designated location -- a feature not supported by existing Fractal and Harco markers due to their structural and dictionary constraints.

AI.tldr: A recursive ArUco marker design enabling unlimited depth and robust detection under occlusion by embedding inner markers within both black and white bits, while preserving a single dictionary identifier across scales.
AI.motivation: To overcome the limited operational range and occlusion sensitivity of standard fiducial markers, enabling robust, scalable UAV landing zones and multi-agent coordination with a single identifier across recursive scales.
AI.method: Transform any standard ArUco marker into a recursive marker of arbitrary depth using a modified bit-sampling strategy that embeds complete markers within both black and white bits of the parent. The detection pipeline is extended to recover inner markers without requiring the center to be visible, and a single unique ID is maintained across all recursion levels to build a large, extensible dictionary.
AI.result: The approach formally guarantees unlimited recursion depth and robustness to partial occlusion, and enables a shared dictionary with many unique landing pads suitable for fleets of UAVs, outperforming existing fractal and Harco markers in dictionary flexibility and placement constraints.
AI.conclusion: The proposed Recursive ArUco markers offer a scalable, robust fiducial system for autonomous UAV navigation and precision landing, with practical potential for multi-robot coordination and expanded marker dictionaries. Further empirical evaluation would clarify detection speed, error rates, and real-world robustness.

title: Consensus as Privileged Context for Label-Free Self-Distillation
summary: Sampling multiple solutions and returning the majority answer is among the most reliable ways to improve the reasoning accuracy of large language models without labels, and a growing family of methods converts this consensus signal into training supervision. However, existing approaches use consensus only in restricted forms: as a filter that selects solutions for fine-tuning, as a preference between answers, or as a scalar reward for reinforcement learning, discarding most of the information that the agreeing solutions contain. We present CANON (Consensus-ANchored self-distillatiON), a label-free training method that turns consensus into dense, token-level supervision. For each unlabeled prompt, CANON samples multiple solutions, extracts the majority answer, and conditions a frozen snapshot of the model on a solution that reaches it; this consensus-anchored teacher then supervises the model on its own rollouts at every token. Experiments on mathematical and scientific reasoning benchmarks show that CANON improves pass@1 by up to 12 points, outperforming label-free reinforcement learning by 6 points at a seventh of its compute and approaching a teacher conditioned on gold solutions; trained on pooled unlabeled data, it transfers to held-out benchmarks, matching training methods that use gold labels. Analysis suggests that the improvements are not pure distribution sharpening: after training, the model solves problems it previously never solved in 32 attempts, and its majority vote itself becomes more accurate.

AI.tldr: CANON leverages consensus-anchored self-distillation to convert majority-correct solutions from unlabeled prompts into dense, token-level supervision, yielding strong label-free improvements in reasoning tasks.
AI.motivation: To exploit unlabeled data by transforming consensus among multiple sampled solutions into rich supervision, overcoming the limitations of filtering, preference signals, or scalar rewards.
AI.method: For each unlabeled prompt: sample multiple solutions; identify majority answer; condition a frozen snapshot of the model on a solution that reaches that majority; use this consensus-anchored teacher to supervise the model on its own token-level rollouts. Training is label-free and relies on consensus signals.
AI.result: CANON improves pass@1 by up to 12 points on math/science benchmarks; outperforms label-free RL by 6 points at 1/7 compute; approaches performance of a teacher conditioned on gold solutions; transfers to held-out benchmarks when trained on pooled unlabeled data; matches gold-label training methods; analysis suggests improvements exceed distribution sharpening.
AI.conclusion: Consensus-anchored self-distillation is an effective, label-free supervision signal that yields substantive gains in reasoning tasks and robust transfer, with the majority vote becoming more accurate and enabling solutions previously unattainable.

title: T3HG-Editor: Text-driven 3D Human Garment Editing with Body Priors Embedded in SMPL-X
summary: While 3D Gaussian Editing (3DGE) has seen substantial progress, text-driven 3D human garment editing remains largely underexplored. Existing 3DGE works typically follow a paradigm that applies 2D editing techniques to multi-view rendered images and updates 3D Gaussians based on the modified images. Extending such methods to 3D human garment editing suffers from low-fidelity outcomes, caused by introduced distortions and garment inconsistencies. A promising breakthrough opportunity arises from the SMPL eXpressive (SMPL-X) model that embodies rich prior information for virtual humans. Motivated by this insight, we propose a text-driven 3D human garment editor termed T3HG-Editor, which delivers high-fidelity and garment consistent results by leveraging geometry and joint priors embedded in SMPL-X. Specifically, T3HG-Editor contains three stages, namely obtainment of editable Gaussians, garment consistent editing, and Gaussian updating with overflow pruning. The obtainment of editable Gaussians begins with seeding Gaussians along SMPL-X normals to generate sufficient near surface Gaussians, followed by a 2D mask constraint that precisely localizes the target Gaussians to be edited. The garment consistent editing aggregates tokens corresponding to the same SMPL-X vertex across multiple views and propagates them to their original views, enforcing garment consistency without requiring additional training. Gaussian updating with overflow pruning employs a Signed Distance Function (SDF) defined on SMPL-X to construct a human distance field, which is then integrated with a 2D semantic mask to prune overflowing Gaussians, thus preventing contamination of non-target regions. Experiments on multiple subjects and diverse garment types demonstrate that T3HG-Editor outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both editing quality and garment consistency.

AI.tldr: Proposes T3HG-Editor, a text-driven 3D garment editor that leverages SMPL-X priors to produce high-fidelity, garment-consistent edits on 3D Gaussians via a three-stage pipeline.
AI.motivation: Current 3D Gaussian Editing (3DGE) for text-driven garment editing suffers from distortions and inconsistencies when applying 2D edits to multi-view renders. SMPL-X provides rich priors for humans, offering a path to higher fidelity and consistency.
AI.method: Three-stage pipeline: (1) obtainment of editable Gaussians by seeding Gaussians along SMPL-X normals and localizing targets with a 2D mask; (2) garment-consistent editing by aggregating tokens for the same SMPL-X vertex across views and propagating to all views without extra training; (3) Gaussian updating with overflow pruning via an SDF-based human distance field on SMPL-X integrated with a 2D semantic mask to prune overflowing Gaussians and prevent contamination of non-target regions.
AI.result: Experimental results on multiple subjects and diverse garment types show T3HG-Editor outperforms state-of-the-art methods in editing quality and garment consistency.
AI.conclusion: SMPL-X-guided, training-free text-driven 3D garment editing yields higher fidelity and garment-consistent results, robust across subjects and garment types; effective overflow-pruning mechanism enhances localization and quality.

title: Merging Reaction to Cognition: A Hybrid Cognitive Strategy for Odour Source Localisation in Natural Environments
summary: Chemical pollutants released into the environment are transported by turbulent flows, generating complex, intermittent plume structures that threaten ecosystems and human health. Rapid localisation of emission sources is critical, and field robots equipped with chemical sensors provide a viable means to perform this task. However, inferring source location from sensor readings remains difficult due to sparse detections and the absence of reliable concentration gradients. Existing approaches fall into two paradigms. Bio-inspired strategies rely on reactive behaviours triggered by detections, such as surge-casting, offering efficiency but requiring scenario-specific tuning. Cognitive strategies integrate observations into a probabilistic belief over source location. While more robust, they suffer from excessive exploration and strong dependence on belief accuracy. The Fast-Cognitive algorithm reduced this computational burden but preserved the fundamental limitations. Previous Markov chain analysis revealed that source-directed motions occur roughly twice as often following odour detections, indicating that reactive behaviours naturally emerge within cognitive frameworks. This work proposes a hybrid strategy that explicitly incorporates bio-inspired reactivity into belief-dependent motion planning. It introduces a detection-triggered switching mechanism formalising transitions between crossflow exploration and source-directed motion, prioritising source proximity over information gain. Behavioural parameters are derived directly from belief metrics, enabling adaptive reactivity without manual tuning. The approach is validated through simulations under three turbulence conditions and field experiments with an autonomous surface vehicle in the Mondego River, Portugal. Results show up to 50% reduction in travelled distance, 86% success rate, and 3.2m average localisation error.

AI.tldr: Hybrid detection-triggered switching integrates bio-inspired reactivity with belief-based motion planning for efficient chemical-source localisation in turbulent plumes.
