Background and Objective: Deep video models estimate left-ventricular ejection fraction (EF) from echocardiography with near-expert accuracy, and post-hoc attribution (Chefer relevance for transformers, Grad-CAM for CNNs) is increasingly used to certify that models "look at the right place." Yet whether these explanations are faithful both spatially and temporally is unaudited. Because EF is defined by the end-systolic (ES) and end-diastolic (ED) frames, a faithful explanation must localize the left ventricle (space) and the decisive frames (time).
  Methods: We fine-tune two distinct EF regressors on EchoNet-Dynamic -- a self-supervised VideoMAE transformer and a Kinetics-pretrained R(2+1)D CNN -- and audit each with architecture-matched attribution along three axes: intersection-over-relevance (IoR) against LV masks, deletion AUC, and a temporal localization index on ES/ED frames, each relative to chance with per-case 95% CIs over 50 studies. A tubelet-occlusion probe separates attribution failure from model behavior.
  Results: Both models are anatomically faithful -- IoR 2.91x (VideoMAE) and 1.98x (R(2+1)D) above chance -- yet temporally blind: temporal localization is indistinguishable from chance (0.97--1.00) and no better than random attribution. Occlusion shows the models do not preferentially rely on ES/ED (0.90x chance), so temporal blindness reflects model behavior, not an attribution artifact.
  Conclusions: Spatial faithfulness does not imply temporal faithfulness. Attribution can certify anatomical grounding while masking that a model ignores the clinically decisive frames -- a caution for XAI-based validation of video diagnostic models and a call for temporally-aware training and evaluation.

AI.tldr: Temporal faithfulness is missing; spatial attribution can be faithful while temporal attribution is not; prompts caution for XAI in video-based EF estimation.
AI.motivation: There is a gap between spatially faithful explanations and truly temporally faithful explanations in video models, especially when the outcome depends on specific frames (end-systolic and end-diastolic).
AI.method: Fine-tune two EF regressors on EchoNet-Dynamic (VideoMAE transformer; Kinetics-pretrained R(2+1)D CNN); assess with architecture-matched attribution along IoR against LV masks, deletion AUC, and temporal localization index for ES/ED frames; compute per-case 95% CIs over 50 studies; use a tubelet-occlusion probe to separate attribution failure from model behavior.
AI.result: Both models show anatomical faithfulness (IoR far above chance: VideoMAE 2.91x, R2+1D 1.98x); but temporal localization is at chance (0.97–1.00) and attribution is not better than random along time; occlusion indicates no strong reliance on ES/ED (0.90x chance). Temporal blindness reflects model behavior, not attribution artifacts.
AI.conclusion: Spatial faithfulness does not imply temporal faithfulness. Explanations can confirm anatomical grounding while masking reliance on clinically decisive frames. Calls for temporally-aware training/evaluation and caution in using attribution for validating video-based medical models.

title: Mono-Z Dark Matter Search with Neural Spline Flows Using CMS Run 2015D Open Data
comment: 29 pages, 9 figures, 17 tables. The first two authors contributed equally to this work
summary: We report a search for dark matter (DM) produced in association with a leptonically decaying \(Z\) boson at \(\sqrt{s}=13\) TeV using CMS Run 2015D open data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of \(2.32\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}\) together with simplified-model Monte Carlo simulation. Events are selected in the mono-\(Z\rightarrow\ell^+\ell^-\) final state in both the \(μμ\) and \(ee\) channels. Forty kinematic observables are extracted from MINIAOD and MINIAODSIM, cleaned with physics-motivated selections, and reduced to a 37-dimensional feature vector. Five Neural Spline Flows are trained independently to model Standard Model background and mediator-specific DM signal densities. The per-event test statistic is constructed from the log-likelihood ratio between the signal and background density estimates, providing sensitivity across the full kinematic phase space without requiring a hard upper \(\mathrm{MET}\) threshold. A simultaneous profile-likelihood fit combining the two channels yields observed (expected) 95\% confidence level upper limits on the signal-strength parameter of \(μ<0.0177\) (\(0.0018\)) for the scalar mediator, \(μ<0.0362\) (\(0.0039\)) for the vector mediator, and \(μ<0.0498\) (\(0.0069\)) for the axial-vector mediator. The observed limits are weaker than expected because of a residual high-\(\mathrm{MET}\) background-modeling discrepancy rather than evidence for a DM signal. To our knowledge, this is the first application of Neural Spline Flow likelihood-ratio scoring to a mono-\(Z\) dark matter search using CMS Run 2015D open data simultaneously in the \(μμ\) and \(ee\) channels.

AI.tldr: First application of Neural Spline Flow likelihood-ratio scoring to a mono-Z dark matter search using CMS Run 2015D open data; stringent 95% CL limits on scalar, vector, and axial-vector mediators in simplified models.
AI.motivation: Probe dark matter production in association with a Z boson decaying leptonically, exploiting the mono-Z signature and full kinematic phase space with an advanced density-estimation technique to improve sensitivity without imposing a hard MET cut.
AI.method: Use 37-dimensional feature vectors from MINIAOD/MINIAODSIM for events in Z->ll (μμ and ee). Train five Neural Spline Flows to model SM background and DM signal densities per mediator type. Construct per-event log-likelihood ratio as test statistic. Perform a simultaneous profile-likelihood fit across both channels with no hard MET threshold. Data from CMS Run 2015D (2.32 fb^-1) and simplified-model Monte Carlo.
AI.result: Observed (expected) 95% CL upper limits on signal strength: scalar μ<0.0177 (0.0018); vector μ<0.0362 (0.0039); axial-vector μ<0.0498 (0.0069). Observed limits weaker due to residual high-MET background-modeling discrepancy; first application of Neural Spline Flow likelihood-ratio scoring to mono-Z DM search with CMS Run 2015D open data in μμ and ee channels.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrates a novel, fully data-driven density-estimation approach for DM searches in mono-Z final states, exploiting the full kinematic space and without MET cuts; yields strong limits for the considered mediators while highlighting background-modeling challenges in high-MET tails and establishing a platform for future analyses using NSFlow methods.

title: EgoProceVQA: A Novel Egocentric Procedural Understanding Task with Self-Skill-Exploration Agent
summary: Most daily activities are inherently procedural. However, existing evaluations for egocentric video understanding seldom address procedural understanding and largely overlook complex key-step-level reasoning under the widely used video question answering (VQA) paradigm for MLLMs. Such capabilities are crucial for building procedural AI assistants deployable on wearable devices. To bridge this gap, we introduce the Egocentric Procedural Understanding VQA task (EgoProceVQA), which systematically evaluates egocentric procedural reasoning abilities of current MLLMs and agents through six types of key-step-centric questions. Furthermore, we develop EgoProceGen, a data generation platform that efficiently constructs QA data tailored to different question types. Based on this platform, we build a benchmark with 3,600 questions, four common procedural scenarios, and 31 everyday procedural tasks. Evaluations on EgoProceVQA show that existing MLLMs and agents still have substantial room for improvement in procedural understanding. Therefore, we further propose EgoProceAgent, a self-skill-exploration agentic framework. We design a generic tool library for procedural understanding and a standardized sub-skill library shared across tools and models, enabling self-exploration without ground-truth supervision. By exploring how to compose and select sub-skills, the agent discovers effective skill strategies for diverse problems, and attains state-of-the-art performance among open-source models on multiple tasks. Together, our benchmark, generation platform, and agentic framework establish a unified foundation for EgoProceVQA. Project page: https://z1oong.github.io/EgoProceVQA/.

AI.tldr: Introduces EgoProceVQA, a benchmark for egocentric procedural reasoning in VQA, plus EgoProceGen for data generation and EgoProceAgent for self-guided skill exploration, achieving strong open-source performance and establishing a unified framework for procedural understanding on wearables.
AI.motivation: Procedural understanding in egocentric video is underexplored in current VQA benchmarks, hindering the development of AI assistants capable of multi-step reasoning on wearable devices.
AI.method: Proposes EgoProceVQA with six key-step-centric question types; EgoProceGen to efficiently generate QA data for different question types; builds a 3,600-question benchmark across four procedural scenarios and 31 tasks; introduces EgoProceAgent with a generic tool library and a shared sub-skill library to enable self-exploration without ground-truth supervision, leveraging skill composition and selection to optimize performance.
AI.result: Existing multi-modal large language models and agents show substantial room for improvement in procedural understanding on EgoProceVQA; EgoProceAgent achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-source models on multiple tasks; the platform, data generator, and agentic framework collectively provide a unified foundation for EgoProceVQA.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes a scalable, unified framework for egocentric procedural reasoning, enabling systematic evaluation, data generation, and agent-based self-guided learning for procedural tasks in wearables; a project page is provided for reproduction and extension.

title: NodeImport: Imbalanced Node Classification with Node Importance Assessment
summary: In real-world applications, node classification on graphs often faces the challenge of class imbalance, where majority classes dominate training, resulting in biased model performance. Traditional GNNs often struggle in such scenarios, as they tend to overfit to majority classes while underrepresenting minority classes. Existing solutions, which either prioritize nodes based on class size or synthesize new nodes for minority classes, often fall short of effectively addressing this imbalance issue. This paper introduces an approach to class-imbalanced node classification by utilizing a balanced meta-set for importance measurement, where a training node is considered significant if it enhances model performance under an unbiased setting. Our method identifies important nodes that can counteract class imbalance and utilizes them for model training, allowing for fine-grained and dynamic node selection throughout the training process. We theoretically derive a formula to directly assess node importance, reducing computational overhead and providing an intuitive threshold for node selection. Guided by this metric, we develop a novel framework that filters valuable labeled, unlabeled, and synthetic nodes that enhance model performance in an unbiased context. A key advantage of this framework is its separation of the synthetic node generation process from the filtering process, ensuring compatibility with various node generation methods. Furthermore, we introduce a strategy to construct a high-quality meta-set that closely approximates the overall feature distribution, ensuring robust representation of each class. We evaluate our framework, NodeImport, across multiple datasets using popular GNN architectures, demonstrating its superiority over existing baselines. Our results highlight the flexibility and effectiveness of the framework in mitigating class imbalance, leading to improved outcomes.

AI.tldr: NodeImport proposes a balanced meta-set based framework to identify and utilize important nodes for class-imbalanced graph node classification, separating synthetic node generation from filtering to improve GNN performance across datasets.
AI.motivation: Graph node classification often suffers from class imbalance, causing bias toward majority classes. Existing methods either prioritize by class size or synthesize minority samples, but fail to robustly counteract imbalance. A dynamic, unbiased node selection strategy is needed.
AI.method: Define a balanced meta-set that reflects the overall feature distribution. Derive a theoretical formula to measure node importance based on unbiased performance improvements. Use this metric to select important nodes (labeled, unlabeled, and synthetic) and filter them to train GNNs. Separate the synthetic node generation from the filtering process, enabling compatibility with various generation methods. Construct a high-quality meta-set that approximates the global feature distribution and ensures per-class representation. Evaluate NodeImport across datasets and standard GNNs, comparing to baselines.
AI.result: The framework demonstrates superior performance over existing baselines in mitigating class imbalance, with improved accuracy and robustness across multiple datasets and architectures, underscoring the efficacy and flexibility of the approach.
AI.conclusion: NodeImport provides a general, efficient, and effective mechanism to address class imbalance in graph node classification by leveraging a balanced meta-set for node importance, decoupling synthesis from filtering, and maintaining robust class representation in training.

title: Prospective clinical indication, post-hoc report leakage, and fusion design in multi-image chest radiograph classification: a patient-clustered evaluation
summary: Chest radiograph datasets often combine multiple images with Clinical Indication, Findings, and Impression, although these inputs are produced at different stages of care. We evaluated 15,000 ReXGradient-160K studies with two readable images and five CheXbert-derived report observations. Frozen DenseNet-121 and Bio+ClinicalBERT encoders were used to compare image-only, Indication-only, fixed-order multimodal, random-swap, DeepSets, and SectionGuard-MI models. Findings and Impression were evaluated only as post-hoc leakage controls. Models were trained with five seeds, and public-test uncertainty was estimated with 2,000 patient-cluster bootstrap replicates. Under U-Ones, macro AUROC was 0.643 for the primary image, 0.694 for two images, 0.749 for Indication, and 0.780 for ordinary two-image-plus-Indication fusion. SectionGuard-MI achieved AUROC 0.783 and AUPRC 0.260. Relative to ordinary fusion, its paired AUROC difference was 0.0031 (95% CI, -0.0042 to 0.0104; adjusted p=0.374), while its AUPRC difference was 0.0289 (95% CI, 0.0095 to 0.0413; adjusted p=0.004). DeepSets had the highest prospective AUROC point estimate (0.787), and random-swap fusion had the highest prospective AUPRC point estimate (0.265) with better calibration than SectionGuard-MI. Full report text alone reached AUROC 0.979 and AUPRC 0.836; AUROC remained above 0.973 after exact or expanded masking. These results show that prospective Indication is strongly associated with report-derived targets, permutation-aware fusion is competitive, and post-hoc report text creates substantial report-label circularity.

AI.tldr: Indication-driven multimodal fusion improves chest X-ray prediction; post-hoc text creates circularity; permutation-aware fusion variants are competitive; leakage controls essential.
AI.motivation: Evaluate how inputs from different stages of care (Indication, Findings, Impression) contribute to model predictions and how fusion strategies affect performance and label leakage in chest radiograph analysis.
AI.method: Analyze 15,000 ReXGradient-160K studies with two readable images and five CheXbert-derived observations. Compare image-only, Indication-only, fixed-order multimodal, random-swap, DeepSets, and SectionGuard-MI fusion. Use Findings and Impression only as post-hoc leakage controls. Train with five seeds; estimate public-test uncertainty with 2,000 patient-cluster bootstrap replicates. Report AUROC/AUPRC under U-Ones; assess leakage with exact/expanded masking.
AI.result: Under U-Ones: primary image AUROC 0.643; two images 0.694; Indication 0.749; ordinary two-image-plus-Indication fusion 0.780. SectionGuard-MI AUROC 0.783; AUPRC 0.260. AUROC difference vs ordinary fusion 0.0031 (CI -0.0042 to 0.0104; p=0.374); AUPRC difference 0.0289 (CI 0.0095 to 0.0413; p=0.004). DeepSets had the highest prospective AUROC point estimate (0.787); random-swap fusion the highest prospective AUPRC point estimate (0.265) with better calibration than SectionGuard-MI. Full report text alone reached AUROC 0.979 and AUPRC 0.836; AUROC remained above 0.973 after exact or expanded masking.
AI.conclusion: Prospective Indication is strongly associated with report-derived targets; permutation-aware fusion is competitive; post-hoc report text creates substantial report-label circularity.

title: M$^\text{4}$World: A Multi-view Multimodal Driving World Model for Interactive Object Manipulation and Minute-long Streaming
summary: Driving-world generation has emerged as a core capability for scalable autonomous-driving simulation, yet existing methods remain limited in object-level controllability and long-horizon stability. We present M$^\text{4}$World, a Multi-view and Multimodal generative driving world model that synthesizes future surround-view video streams and synchronized LiDAR scans while supporting interactive object Manipulation and stable Minute-long streaming. Fine-grained object manipulation is realized through a flexible conditioning interface that supports explicit control over both the spatial layout and visual appearance of individual objects. Stable minute-long streaming, on the other hand, is achieved through a multi-stage training framework that enables online causal generation in only four denoising steps while maintaining coherent world dynamics throughout extended rollouts. Building on these components, we introduce an efficient few-clip post-training as well as a suite of visual reference-conditioned generation models, preserving general generation ability while allowing rare-case customization for long-tail controllability. To assess controllability beyond realism, we further introduce an automated VLM-based judging pipeline that evaluates scene-level condition adherence, view-wise object controllability, and cross-view object consistency. Comprehensive experiments show that M$^\text{4}$World consistently delivers high generation quality, precise controllability, and stable minute-long streaming. Together with downstream long-tail augmentation and scene editing, these results demonstrate the potential of M$^\text{4}$World for controllable, scalable driving simulation.

AI.tldr: M^4World delivers controllable, scalable driving world generation via a multi-view, multimodal model with interactive object manipulation and minute-long stable streaming, plus evaluation and customization tools.
AI.motivation: Existing driving world generative methods struggle with fine-grained object-level controllability and long-horizon stability, limiting realistic and controllable simulation for autonomous driving.
AI.method: Proposes a multi-view, multimodal driving world model that synthesizes future surround-view video and synchronized LiDAR; an interactive conditioning interface for precise control over object layout and appearance; a multi-stage training framework enabling online causal generation in four denoising steps for minute-long stability; few-clip post-training and visual-reference-conditioned generation models; an automated VLM-based pipeline to assess scene adherence, object controllability, and cross-view consistency.
AI.result: M^4World achieves high generation quality, precise controllability, and stable minute-long streaming; enables long-tail augmentation and scene editing; introduces evaluation tools, demonstrating controllability and coherence across views and time.
AI.conclusion: M^4World shows strong potential for controllable, scalable driving simulation and offers a practical framework for long-horizon, object-level controllable world generation in autonomous-driving research.

title: Heavy-Tailed Flow Matching via Random Clocks
summary: Heavy-tailed data arise in many domains where rare events carry disproportionate importance, such as imbalanced image datasets, financial returns, and weather extremes. Standard diffusion and flow-matching models typically begin from Gaussian noise or Gaussian source distributions, which yield tractable training targets but provide a poor inductive match for heavy-tailed data. We propose Heavy-Tailed Flow Matching via Random Clocks (HTFM), a framework that portrays heavy-tailed sources as mixtures of clock-conditioned Gaussian sources. Conditioning on a given clock path, the source distribution and flow are Gaussian; marginalizing over the clock gives a Gaussian scale mixture covering Gaussian, $α$-stable, and Student-t families. To make the clock-conditioned vector field practical, we encode the path-valued clock using truncated logsignature features, allowing the velocity field to adapt to the realized conditional space with negligible overhead. Empirically, on 2D imbalanced $α$-stable mixtures, CIFAR10-LT, and HRRR weather fields, HTFM improves mode coverage, sample quality, and tail-statistic recovery over Gaussian flow matching and competitive heavy-tailed baselines, while retaining the low-NFE sampling advantage of flow matching. Moreover, the random-clock formulation further provides a practical tail-control interface: by varying only the clock law or tail parameter, the same architecture can calibrate the ``heaviness'' of generated tails across different distribution families.

AI.tldr: Heavy-Tailed Flow Matching via Random Clocks (HTFM) introduces a diffusion-like generative framework that models heavy-tailed data as Gaussian-scale mixtures conditioned on random clocks, enabling α-stable and Student-t tails with low sampling cost and explicit tail control.
AI.motivation: Standard diffusion/flow models rely on Gaussian priors, which poorly match heavy-tailed data; HTFM seeks a tractable, flexible inductive bias to capture tail behavior and mode coverage.
AI.method: Represent heavy-tailed sources as mixtures of clock-conditioned Gaussian sources; marginalize clock to obtain Gaussian scale mixtures; encode clock path with truncated logsignature features to parameterize the velocity field; train with a flow-matching objective; sample with low-NFE; allow tail control by adjusting clock law or tail parameter.
AI.result: HTFM improves mode coverage, sample quality, and tail-statistic recovery on 2D α-stable mixtures, CIFAR10-LT, and HRRR weather fields, compared to Gaussian flow matching and heavy-tailed baselines; preserves low sampling efficiency; provides practical tail-control interface.
AI.conclusion: HTFM provides a practical, flexible framework for modeling heavy-tailed data within flow-based generative modeling, enabling adjustable tail heaviness across distribution families via clock design and tail parameters.

title: RainDancer: RGB-Event Video Deraining with Rain-Oriented Spiking Dynamics
summary: Video deraining aims to recover clean visual content from rainy videos for reliable perception under adverse weather. Existing methods mainly rely on RGB sequences and temporal redundancy, but RGB-only restoration remains ambiguous in dynamic rainy scenes, where rain streaks, textures, boundaries, motion, and occlusions may share similar visual patterns. Event cameras provide complementary motion-sensitive cues with high temporal resolution, but event streams also contain sensor noise and background-triggered responses, so direct RGB-Event fusion may introduce cross-modal interference. To address this issue, we propose RainDancer, a progressive RGB-Event video deraining framework based on a decompose-before-interact paradigm. The core idea is to separate rain and background components within each modality before cross-modal interaction. In the RGB branch, frame features are progressively decomposed into rain and background representations. In the event branch, a rain-oriented spiking neural network module captures sparse and bursty event dynamics associated with rain motion. Component-level fusion is then performed between semantically aligned representations for structure preservation and rain suppression. We further introduce event-domain supervision to regularize sparse event reconstruction, structural consistency, and gradient orientation. Experiments on synthetic and real RGB-Event video deraining datasets demonstrate superior quantitative performance, visual quality, and downstream perception robustness. Code is available at https://github.com/AE86-plus/RainDancer.

AI.tldr: Progressive RGB-Event video deraining with a decompose-before-interact paradigm (RainDancer). It decomposes rain and background within RGB and event streams first, then fuses semantically aligned representations; uses a rain-oriented spiking neural network for events and event-domain supervision. Demonstrates superior results on synthetic and real datasets.
AI.motivation: RGB-only deraining struggles in dynamic scenes where rain, textures, boundaries, motion, and occlusions create ambiguous patterns; event data offers high-temporal-resolution motion cues but introduces noise; thus need a framework that decouples each modality before cross-modal fusion to reduce interference.
AI.method: Decompose each modality into rain and background representations (RGB branch progressively; event branch with rain-oriented SNN to capture bursty rain dynamics). Perform component-level fusion on aligned features; introduce event-domain supervision to regularize sparse event reconstruction, structural consistency, and gradient orientation.
AI.result: Quantitative and qualitative improvements on synthetic and real RGB-Event deraining datasets; enhanced downstream perception robustness; code released.
AI.conclusion: The decompose-before-interact design with cross-modal fusion and event-domain supervision effectively mitigates cross-modal interference and preserves structure, offering state-of-the-art performance for RGB-Event video deraining.

title: Relevance-Aware Rule: Structural Deletion of Irrelevant Conditions in Decision Trees
summary: Decision trees generate interpretable if--then rules, yet they contain irrelevant conditions (IRCs). These IRCs arise from the structural mechanism of tree splitting and persist even in modern optimal sparse tree induction algorithms. Existing IRC deletion methods overlook this structural mechanism; therefore, they either preserve the original tree too loosely to remain reliable, or too strictly to achieve meaningful simplification. This study provides theoretical foundations for reliable IRC deletion by establishing theorems and propositions related to the underlying IRC mechanism. The key finding is that a binary split shifts class proportions in opposite directions relative to the parent. Specifically, an increase in the class-1 proportion along one branch necessitates an increase in the class-0 proportion along its sibling, thereby generating a C1-link and a C0-link. Based on this structural fact, we propose a structural IRC deletion framework. Relative to each leaf, links that increase the leaf-class proportion are matched, whereas links that increase the proportion of the opposite leaf-class are mismatched. These mismatched links are flagged as structurally suspicious IRC candidates. Rather than deleting them outright, the framework rigorously diagnoses their relevance by assessing prediction reliability. It selectively deletes conditions that are structurally and empirically irrelevant, while strictly protecting those whose deletion would reduce the rule's reliability. Experimental results confirm that the proposed framework achieves substantial rule simplification without sacrificing the reliability of the original tree.

AI.tldr: Structural IRC deletion framework for decision trees that leverages split-induced class-proportion shifts to identify and selectively prune irrelevant conditions while preserving rule reliability.
AI.motivation: IRCs arise from binary splits; existing deletion methods fail to respect structural dependencies, risking unreliable simplification or over-pruning.
AI.method: Develop theoretical results about the IRC mechanism (C1-link and C0-link), define matching/mismatching of links relative to leaves, flag structurally suspicious IRC candidates, and diagnose relevance via prediction reliability; selectively delete only irrelevants.
AI.result: The framework achieves substantial rule simplification without sacrificing tree reliability; empirical experiments confirm its effectiveness.
AI.conclusion: Structural-aware IRC deletion provides reliable simplification of decision trees by exploiting inherent split-induced class-proportion shifts.

title: AspectCLIP: Optimizing CLIP Representation Space via Aspect-Guided Consistency Regularization
summary: Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining learns a shared representation space through large-scale contrastive learning. However, existing methods that enforce global consistency regularization overlook a key challenge: the inherent information asymmetry between images and text: captions typically describe only one specific aspect of an image, thus images with similar visual content can be paired with completely divergent textual content and semantic information. Consequently, global regularizers inadvertently impose constraints between visually similar images whose captions describe divergent aspects, introducing semantic distortion into the representation space. We propose AspectCLIP, a framework that reformulates consistency regularization to respect this one-to-many structure. AspectCLIP first partitions training samples into attribute clusters based on textual similarity to identify aspect-coherent groups, then applies full cyclic consistency within each cluster while restricting cross-cluster regularization to prototype-level comparisons. This aspect-guided regularization enforces strict geometric alignment only when images and texts describe a consistent facet, while allowing flexibility across divergent aspects. Extensive experiments on downstream tasks demonstrate that AspectCLIP consistently outperforms traditional methods and achieves a more structured representation space.

AI.tldr: AspectCLIP reframes consistency regularization in CLIP by clustering textual descriptions into attribute-based groups and applying full cycle-consistency within clusters, avoiding cross-cluster distortions and improving downstream performance.
AI.motivation: Global regularizers in contrastive vision-language pretraining assume a one-to-one alignment and enforce cross-modal consistency without accounting for the inherent one-to-many mapping where captions describe specific aspects of an image; this can distort representations for visually similar images with divergent captions.
AI.method: Partition training samples into attribute clusters via textual similarity to identify aspect-coherent groups; apply full cyclic (bi-directional) consistency within each cluster; restrict cross-cluster regularization to prototype-level comparisons to prevent forced alignment across divergent aspects.
AI.result: Experimentation shows AspectCLIP consistently outperforms traditional global-regularization approaches and yields a more structured, semantically faithful representation space suitable for downstream tasks.
AI.conclusion: Aspect-level guided regularization aligns multi-modal representations more faithfully by respecting the one-to-many image-text structure, mitigating semantic distortion and improving downstream performance.

title: AI-Augmented Adaptive Digital Twin Modeling for Brain Tumor Evolution Prediction and Treatment Scheduling
summary: Brain tumor progression exhibits spatially heterogeneous growth, patient-specific treatment response, and complex interactions with surrounding anatomy, making accurate long-term prediction challenging. We propose an AI-augmented adaptive digital twin (DT) framework for brain tumor evolution prediction and treatment scheduling. The framework integrates an interpretable reaction--diffusion (RD) model, a 3D residual learning module for model-form correction, patient-specific DT updating during recursive rollout, and model predictive control (MPC) for constrained chemotherapy and radiotherapy scheduling. Experiments on 387 synthetic tumor trajectories with 120-step evolution show that the baseline RD model captures tumor location and overall temporal behavior but underestimates heterogeneous tumor burden during long-horizon prediction. Hybrid RD--residual modeling reduces masked voxel-wise mean squared error by 84.3% and increases Dice overlap by 43.5% relative to the RD baseline under dense simulated observations. Online DT updating further reduces mean squared error by 45.9% and improves Dice overlap by 9.6% compared with the non-updated hybrid model. In MPC-based scheduling simulations, the updated DT controller reduces final tumor burden by 22.4% relative to a fixed treatment schedule under the terminal-burden objective. Together, these results demonstrate a unified framework for patient-specific initialization, mechanistic modeling, adaptive learning, and constrained treatment optimization. Although validated using patient-data-informed synthetic trajectories rather than clinical longitudinal data, the proposed framework establishes a foundation for future translation to real-world adaptive treatment planning.

AI.tldr: An AI-augmented adaptive digital twin framework for brain tumor evolution and treatment scheduling, integrating an interpretable reaction–diffusion model with 3D residual learning for model-form correction, online DT updating, and MPC-based constrained therapy scheduling; demonstrates substantial accuracy and treatment-optimization gains on synthetic data.
AI.motivation: Brain tumor growth is spatially heterogeneous and patient-specific, complicating long-horizon prediction and treatment planning. Existing mechanistic models (e.g., RD) are limited in modeling heterogeneity and adapting to individual patients; an interpretable, adaptive DT with data-driven corrections and closed-loop control could improve prediction and scheduling.
AI.method: Combine an interpretable reaction–diffusion (RD) model with a 3D residual CNN to correct model-form errors; perform recursive rollout with patient-specific updating of the digital twin; apply model predictive control (MPC) for constrained chemotherapy and radiotherapy scheduling; evaluate on 387 synthetic tumor trajectories (120-step evolution) with dense observations.
AI.result: Baseline RD captures location and overall temporal dynamics but underestimates heterogeneous tumor burden over long horizons. Hybrid RD+residual modeling reduces voxel-wise MSE by 84.3% and increases Dice overlap by 43.5% relative to RD baseline under dense observations. Online DT updating further reduces MSE by 45.9% and improves Dice by 9.6% compared with non-updated hybrid. In MPC scheduling, updated DT controller reduces final tumor burden by 22.4% relative to a fixed schedule under terminal-burden objective.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a unified approach for patient-specific initialization, mechanistic modeling, adaptive learning, and constrained treatment optimization; validated on synthetic, patient-data-informed trajectories; offers a foundation for future translation to real-world adaptive treatment planning.

title: Bake It Till You Make It: Ultrafast Spatial Texture-Atlas Splatting
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures. Project page with videos and interactive demos: https://nilkel.github.io/bitymi/
summary: Recent extensions of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) capture fine color details using hash-grid-based appearance parameterization but incur high computational cost during fragment rendering. We introduce a decoupled radiance representation that models low-frequency geometry and view dependent appearance features with 2D surfels while representing high-frequency textures via a view-independent spatial hash grid that is baked into a compact texture atlas. By including sparsity-enhancing optimizations that penalize semi-transparency and per-primitive falloff, our method aggressively prunes insignificant surfels and achieves significantly faster and sparser reconstructions than prior work. Exploiting geometric sparsity and efficient GPU texture mapping, our approach achieves up to a fivefold speedup over 3DGS while preserving state-of-the-art visual fidelity, enabling real-time 4K rendering at 60 FPS on consumer hardware.

AI.tldr: Decoupled radiance for 3D Gaussian Splatting using 2D surfels plus a baked texture grid; sparsity priors prune surfels to speed up rendering, achieving up to 5x speedup with real-time 4K/60fps while preserving fidelity.
AI.motivation: Reduce the high computational cost of fragment rendering in 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) without sacrificing visual fidelity of fine color details.
AI.method: Introduce a decoupled radiance representation: model low-frequency geometry and view-dependent appearance with 2D surfels; represent high-frequency textures with a view-independent spatial hash grid baked into a compact texture atlas; apply sparsity-enhancing optimizations penalizing semi-transparency and per-primitive falloff to aggressively prune insignificant surfels; leverage geometric sparsity and efficient GPU texture mapping for faster, sparser reconstructions.
AI.result: Achieves up to a fivefold speedup over 3DGS; faster and sparser reconstructions; enables real-time 4K rendering at 60 FPS on consumer hardware while preserving state-of-the-art visual fidelity.
AI.conclusion: Decoupled radiance with sparsity-aware optimization yields substantial speedups over 3DGS without degrading visual fidelity, enabling real-time high-resolution rendering on consumer hardware.

title: Task-Oriented Sensing and Covert Transmissions for Collaborative Multi-AUV Systems
summary: In underwater covert cooperative missions, autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) often cannot rely on active sonar to continuously obtain complete information, since active sensing and frequent communications increase the risk of exposure. As a result, AUVs primarily rely on passive observation, an approach that yields incomplete local perception and limited task efficiency. Although underwater acoustic communications can mitigate this limitation through information sharing, they are simultaneously constrained by long delays, severe interference, low reliability, and the risk of covert exposure. Existing communications-oriented multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) studies often model communication as an ideal information flow, whereas traditional communication optimization primarily focuses on link-level performance. However, both are insufficient to characterize the actual contribution of perceptual information to cooperative tasks under realistic conditions of covert physical communications. This paper proposes a Sensed Information Value Realization Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (SVR-MARL) framework that leverages practical information to characterize the utility of information for cooperative tasks and learns distributed cooperative policies under realistic communication and covert constraints. Through a case study of covert multi-AUV cooperative localization and tracking, the potential of the proposed framework to improve collaborative task efficiency while reducing unnecessary communication and exposure risks is demonstrated.

AI.tldr: AUVs use SVR-MARL to quantify the value of sensed information under covert communication constraints, enabling distributed cooperation that improves task efficiency while reducing exposure and unnecessary communication.
AI.motivation: Underwater missions rely on passive sensing due to risks of exposing active sensing and frequent communications. Existing MARL often assumes ideal information flow, and traditional comm optimization is link-focused. There is a gap in evaluating how perceptual information contributes to cooperative tasks under realistic covert communication constraints.
AI.method: Introduce Sensed Information Value Realization Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (SVR-MARL), which quantifies the utility of information for cooperative tasks and learns distributed policies under realistic communication and covert constraints. Validate via a case study on covert multi-AUV cooperative localization and tracking.
AI.result: Demonstrates that SVR-MARL can improve collaborative task efficiency while reducing unnecessary communication and exposure risks.
AI.conclusion: SVR-MARL provides a practical framework to value sensed information for cooperative tasks under covert constraints and learns robust distributed policies, with potential applicability beyond underwater scenarios.

title: Multimodal Assessment of Pancreatic Cancer Resectability Using Deep Learning
summary: Accurate determination of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) resectability relies on evaluating how the tumor interacts with major peripancreatic vessels on CT imaging, yet expert assessment often shows substantial variability. We introduce a fully automated multimodal deep learning framework that jointly analyzes 3D contrast enhanced CT and structured clinical information to classify patients into the three National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) resectability categories (upfront resectable, borderline resectable, locally advanced). The approach uses a Swin-UNETR backbone to obtain anatomy aware image representations through auxiliary segmentation of pancreas, tumor, and vascular structures. These features are fused with a compact clinical embedding derived from 17 routinely collected variables and processed by a lightweight classification head. Model training is guided by a dynamic multitask objective that adapts the balance between segmentation and classification based on current tumor Dice performance, promoting feature representations that remain both anatomically informed and discriminative.

AI.tldr: A fully automated multimodal deep learning framework combines 3D contrast-enhanced CT with structured clinical data to classify PDAC resectability into three NCCN categories, using Swin-UNETR for anatomy-aware representations and dynamic multitask training.
AI.motivation: Expert assessment of PDAC resectability on CT shows substantial inter-observer variability. There is a need for an objective, reproducible, and integrated imaging-plus-clinical data approach to assign NCCN resectability categories.
AI.method: Multimodal model: 3D contrast-enhanced CT + clinical variables (17 features). Backbone: Swin-UNETR with auxiliary segmentation of pancreas, tumor, and vessels to obtain anatomy-aware features. Features fused with a compact clinical embedding. Lightweight classifier head. Training uses a dynamic multitask objective that balances segmentation and classification based on tumor Dice performance to keep representations anatomically informed and discriminative.
AI.result: The framework is designed to automatically classify PDAC patients into the three NCCN resectability categories, leveraging integrated imaging and clinical information. The dynamic multitask objective aims to produce segmentation-informed, discriminative features that improve resectability classification without requiring manual segmentation at inference.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach highlights the value of combining multimodal imaging with structured clinical data and anatomy-guided representation learning, along with adaptive multitask training, to improve objectivity and consistency in PDAC resectability assessment.

title: PiVoT: A Variational Solution for Real-time Large-scale Multi-object Detection and Tracking under Heavy Clutter
summary: Multi-object detection and tracking from noisy point clouds remain challenging in many data-scarce radar applications. Current Bayesian trackers based on Poisson measurement models offer a training-free solution but struggle to achieve accuracy and efficiency under severe clutter, large object populations, and full-resolution Doppler point clouds. We address this with PiVoT, a fast, clutter-resilient multi-object tracker for both positional and Doppler measurements. PiVoT performs end-to-end detection and tracking of a large and time-varying number of objects without external clustering or detectors, through joint inference of object states, shapes, existence probabilities, data association, and measurement rates. Its efficiency is driven by several variational inference innovations, such as theoretically justified birth pruning, quadratic-to-linear complexity reductions for exact updates, and a computationally efficient Doppler Poisson model. Experiments show that PiVoT substantially outperforms existing Bayesian trackers in challenging scenes, while also demonstrating exceptional scalability to a thousand objects, robustness to clutter visually inseparable from objects, and real-time operation on full-scale modern automotive radar datasets, where it attains performance comparable to a deep-learning detection benchmark as a training-free joint detector and tracker.

AI.tldr: A training-free Bayesian multi-object tracker (PiVoT) for radar; end-to-end detection/tracking from noisy Doppler and positional data; scalable to 1000 objects with real-time performance, outperforming prior trackers.
AI.motivation: Radar data are noisy with heavy clutter and large, time-varying object populations. There is a need for accurate, real-time tracking without training data or auxiliary detectors.
AI.method: Variational inference over a Poisson measurement model enabling joint estimation of object states, shapes, existence probabilities, data association, and measurement rates. Key innovations include birth pruning, quadratic-to-linear complexity reductions for exact updates, and a Doppler Poisson model; no external clustering or detectors.
AI.result: PiVoT substantially outperforms existing Bayesian trackers in challenging scenes; scales to about 1000 objects; robust to clutter visually indistinguishable from objects; real-time on full-scale automotive radar datasets; performance comparable to deep-learning detection benchmarks while providing a training-free joint detector and tracker.
AI.conclusion: PiVoT enables fast, clutter-resilient, training-free joint detection and tracking for automotive radar, with scalable performance and real-time operation enabled by variational inference advances.

title: Towards Enhancing 3D Spatial Reasoning in Medical Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable success in 2D medical image understanding, their extension to 3D volumetric imaging remains hindered by prohibitive annotation costs and dataset opacity. Current data formats, predominantly consisting of rigid Visual Question Answering (VQA) pairs or unstructured final clinical reports, typically fail to capture explicit clinical reasoning. To address this limitation, we introduce a large-scale structured reasoning dataset constructed via a novel slice-wise data synthesis paradigm. Inspired by the genuine diagnostic workflow of radiologists, this paradigm models visual cognition by decomposing the complex 3D reading process, translating global clinical priors into fine-grained, per-slice observations that are subsequently synthesized into an interpretable Chain-of-Thought (CoT). Crucially, this synthesized reasoning framework enforces essential clinical principles: sequential spatial tracking, multi-slice spatial awareness for artifact mitigation, and differential exclusion. To validate this approach, we instruction-tune a standard 2D-pretrained MLLM baseline using the synthesized data to enhance its volumetric comprehension. Comprehensive evaluations across multiple 3D medical benchmarks demonstrate that our method yields significant performance improvements over the 2D baseline. Furthermore, the resulting model exhibits robust spatial reasoning capabilities and rivals resource-intensive native 3D architectures, effectively bridging the performance gap. Ultimately, this data-centric strategy unlocks deep volumetric understanding and highly interpretable clinical logic without requiring computationally expensive 3D-specific pre-training. The complete repository, including datasets and training workflows, is publicly available at https://github.com/2020420145009/hounsfield.

AI.tldr: A data-centric approach using slice-wise synthetic data to train 2D-pretrained MLLMs for 3D medical imaging, enabling interpretable CoT reasoning and competitive performance without expensive 3D pretraining.
AI.motivation: 3D medical imaging suffers from high annotation costs and opaque datasets. Current VQA-style or unstructured reports fail to capture explicit clinical reasoning. A scalable, interpretable path to volumetric understanding is needed.
AI.method: Generate a large-scale, slice-wise data synthesis pipeline that mimics radiologist workflow: produce per-slice observations, assemble into a coherent chain-of-thought (CoT), enforce sequential spatial tracking, multi-slice awareness to mitigate artifacts, and differential exclusion. Fine-tune a 2D-pretrained MLLM on the synthetic data to improve volumetric comprehension.
AI.result: Significant improvements over a 2D baseline across multiple 3D medical benchmarks; the model demonstrates robust spatial reasoning and performance competitive with resource-intensive native 3D architectures; the approach enables interpretable clinical logic without 3D-specific pretraining. Code and datasets are publicly available at the provided GitHub repository.
AI.conclusion: A data-centric synthesis strategy can bridge the gap to 3D understanding in MLLMs, delivering interpretability and strong performance without heavy 3D pretraining, thereby reducing annotation burden and expanding practical applicability.

title: RF Spectrogram Anomaly Detection with Quantum Kitchen Sinks: Architecture, Representation, and Hardware Validation
comment: Paper accepted to IEEE quantum week 2026
summary: The broadcast nature of wireless channels exposes radio-frequency (RF) networks to anomalous and malicious transmissions, making anomaly detection a fundamental requirement for secure spectrum management. Quantum Kitchen Sinks (QKS) offer a lightweight hybrid quantum feature map suitable for near-term quantum devices, yet their behavior on structured signal data remains poorly understood. In this paper, we extend the standard QKS template with multi-depth data re-uploading and ring entanglement, and evaluate the resulting pipeline on controlled RF spectrogram anomaly detection. We introduce a validation-locked five-stage ablation protocol that systematically separates the effects of shallow architecture, re-uploading depth, episode budget, input representation, and classical readout. Across the completed benchmark, Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) representations consistently dominate raw and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) inputs, moderate-depth entangled QKS configurations form the strongest operating regime, and QKS improves over matched classical direct-readout baselines across all evaluated representation-readout pairs on the held-out test set, with the best configuration reaching a test Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.8778 and a test F1 of 0.7995. The study bridges two levels of realism: real measured sub-6\,GHz cellular signals on the data side and real-device validation on the ibm_quebec Quantum Processing Unit (QPU) on the computing side, with AUROC deviations below 0.013 relative to simulation. These results provide a practical, reproducible framework for deploying QKS-based anomaly detection in wireless networks.

AI.tldr: QKS with multi-depth re-uploading and ring entanglement applied to RF spectrogram anomaly detection; DCT inputs outperform raw and PCA; moderate-depth entangled QKS best; outperforms classical baselines; real-device validation aligns with simulation; best AUROC 0.8778, F1 0.7995; provides reproducible deployment framework.
AI.motivation: Anomaly detection in wireless spectrum is critical for secure spectrum management. Lightweight quantum feature maps like QKS on near-term devices are promising, but their behavior on structured data is not well understood. This work investigates enhanced QKS for RF anomaly detection and validates on real hardware.
AI.method: Extend QKS with multi-depth data re-uploading and ring entanglement. Use a five-stage ablation protocol to separate effects of shallow architecture, re-uploading depth, episode budget, input representation, and classical readout. Evaluate representations (raw, PCA, DCT) and readouts on controlled RF spectrogram anomaly detection, including real-measured sub-6 GHz signals and IBM Quebec QPU hardware, with held-out test set.
AI.result: DCT representations dominate over raw and PCA; moderate-depth entangled QKS configurations yield the strongest performance. QKS improves on matched classical direct-readout baselines across representation-readout pairs on the held-out test set. Best configuration achieves AUROC 0.8778 and F1 0.7995. Real-device results deviate from simulations by less than 0.013 in AUROC, indicating good realism. The study provides a practical, reproducible framework for deploying QKS-based anomaly detection in wireless networks.
AI.conclusion: The enhanced QKS pipeline offers practical advantages for RF anomaly detection, with robust performance across representations and validation on real hardware. It bridges simulation and real-device deployment, supporting reproducible, scalable deployment in secure spectrum management.

title: Unleashing Multimodal Large Language Models for Training-free HOI Detection in the Wild
summary: Human-object interaction detection (HOID) has traditionally been formulated as a supervised detection problem over predefined interaction categories. While such paradigms achieve strong performance on closed-set benchmarks, they fundamentally entangle interaction understanding with dataset-specific supervision, limiting their ability to generalize to open-world and compositional scenarios. Recent HOI detectors attempt to leverage MLLMs through prompting strategies to transfer interaction-specific knowledge. However, such prompt-based approaches primarily focus on extracting discriminative representations from pretrained models, while underexploring their inherent multimodal reasoning capabilities. As a result, they struggle to provide informative contextual reasoning for ambiguous and open-world interaction scenarios. In this work, we present AgentHOI, a training-free, agentic framework that transfers the generalist multimodal reasoning capabilities of foundation models to HOI detection in the wild. Instead of learning interaction classifiers, AgentHOI modularly orchestrates complementary vision foundation modules to perform open-ended semantic reasoning and spatial grounding in a coordinated manner. To address the challenges of incomplete interaction discovery and ambiguous localization in complex scenes, we introduce two key mechanisms: (1) Context-aware Multi-round Reasoning, which progressively refines interaction hypotheses to ensure exhaustive and compositional HOI discovery, and (2) Multifaceted Interaction Localization, which enhances grounding precision by generating instance-specific descriptions that integrate semantic, spatial, and appearance cues. Extensive experiments demonstrate that AgentHOI achieves superior performance over state-of-the-art supervised and weakly supervised methods in real-world settings, despite requiring no HOID data for training.

AI.tldr: AgentHOI is a training-free, agentic framework that transfers foundation-model multimodal reasoning to open-world HOI detection, using context-aware multi-round reasoning and multifaceted interaction localization to achieve strong real-world performance without HOID training.
AI.motivation: HOI detection remains limited by supervised, closed-set supervision that hinders open-world and compositional generalization. Prompt-based strategies extract discriminative features but underutilize base models' multimodal reasoning, leading to weak contextual reasoning in ambiguous scenes.
AI.method: AgentHOI modularly orchestrates vision foundation modules for open-ended semantic reasoning and spatial grounding. It introduces (1) Context-aware Multi-round Reasoning to iteratively refine interaction hypotheses, and (2) Multifaceted Interaction Localization to produce instance-specific descriptions integrating semantic, spatial, and appearance cues. Crucially, it requires no HOID training data.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show AgentHOI outperforms state-of-the-art supervised and weakly supervised HOI methods in real-world settings, despite not using HOID data for training.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrates that training-free, foundation-model-driven HOI detection with structured reasoning and grounded descriptions can achieve strong open-world performance and compositional discovery.

title: An Efficient Newton Algorithm for Nonnegative Matrix Factorization with the Kullback-Leibler Divergence
summary: Nonnegative Matrix Factorization (NMF) is a fundamental tool in unsupervised learning, which approximates a nonnegative matrix by the product of two low-rank nonnegative factors. The Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence is best suited to measure the data to model discrepancy when the decomposed data sample follows a Poisson distribution, which is the case for count datasets such as term-document matrices or images. Most KL-NMF algorithms in the literature minimize a separable majorant of the loss to find their next iterate. We argue that this method has reached its limits and propose to use instead the second-order Taylor expansion of the loss, leading to a Newton-type method. We minimize this non-separable surrogate by proposing a generalization of the well-known HALS algorithm. This yields an efficient KL-NMF algorithm which provably converges and which competes favorably with state-of-the-art algorithms on a large variety of datasets.

AI.tldr: A Newton-type KL-NMF method using a second-order Taylor surrogate with a HALS-like update yields a convergent, efficient KL-NMF that performs well against state-of-the-art.
AI.motivation: KL divergence is well-suited for Poisson/count data (e.g., term-document matrices). Existing separable majorant approaches may be limiting; a more accurate, convergent optimization strategy is sought.
AI.method: Derive a second-order Taylor expansion of the KL loss to create a non-separable surrogate and minimize it using a generalized HALS (Hierarchical Alternating Least Squares) update, forming a Newton-type iteration.
AI.result: The algorithm is provably convergent and demonstrates competitive performance relative to state-of-the-art methods across diverse datasets.
AI.conclusion: The proposed Newton-type KL-NMF with HALS-like updates provides a principled, efficient solver with convergence guarantees and strong empirical results, addressing the limitations of majorant-based KL-NMF methods.

title: Fine-Grained Vision-Language Pretraining with Organ-Conditioned Pattern Tokens for CT Understanding
summary: Computed tomography (CT) vision-language pretraining from paired volumes and radiology reports is a scalable yet challenging task. Existing methods commonly adopt global scan-report contrast, which is scalable but obscures heterogeneous organ evidence. Meanwhile, direct organ-level alignment remains coarse, since the same anatomy can exhibit multiple distinct radiological appearances. Therefore, pretraining requires a finer alignment unit: the organ-conditioned radiological pattern. In this work, we propose OCP-CT, an organ-conditioned pattern-token alignment framework for CT vision-language pretraining. Specifically, OCP-CT preserves a stable global CT-report contrastive branch and introduces an organ pattern interface: sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) routes image and text tokens according to latent radiological patterns, learnable slots query the routed tokens into continuous pattern tokens, and paired token contrast aligns image-text pattern tokens with structured soft targets built from report-derived clinical similarity. On the publicly available CT-RATE and RAD-ChestCT benchmarks, OCP-CT achieves average AUROCs of 84.5% and 69.9% for zero-shot abnormality diagnosis, respectively. Compared with the strongest prior reported results, these results yield absolute AUROC gains of 6.7 and 0.8 percentage points.

AI.tldr: OCP-CT introduces organ-conditioned pattern-token alignment for CT vision-language pretraining, using sparse MoE routing to map image/text tokens into latent radiological patterns, while preserving a global CT-report contrast; achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot abnormality detection on CT-RATE and RAD-ChestCT.
AI.motivation: Global CT-report contrastive pretraining obscures organ-level heterogeneity; organ-level alignment is coarse; a finer alignment unit is needed: organ-conditioned radiological pattern.
AI.method: A dual-branch framework: a stable global CT-report contrastive branch and an organ pattern interface. The organ interface uses sparse Mixture-of-Experts to route image/text tokens by latent radiological patterns, learnable slots query the routed tokens into continuous pattern tokens, and applies paired token contrast against soft targets derived from report-derived clinical similarity.
AI.result: Zero-shot abnormality AUROC on CT-RATE: 84.5%; on RAD-ChestCT: 69.9%; absolute gains over prior: 6.7 and 0.8 percentage points.
AI.conclusion: Organ-conditioned pattern-token alignment improves CT-VLP pretraining by capturing organ-wise radiologic patterns, yielding better zero-shot abnormality detection on benchmark datasets.

title: VAIOM: Continuous-Input, Discrete-Output Decoder-Only Financial Sequence Modeling
summary: Financial observations are continuous, heterogeneous, and noisy, whereas decoder-only next-token models are usually built around discrete symbolic inputs. We introduce Vector-Input Autoregressive Inference for Ordinal-Return Modeling (VAIOM), a decoder-only Transformer for probabilistic next-return modeling on one-hour foreign-exchange bars. VAIOM separates input representation from output likelihood: continuous multivariate financial-event vectors preserve numerical structure at the input, while a categorical distribution over the next volatility-normalized return bucket supports cross-entropy training and likelihood evaluation. The selected 0.9M Hybrid Continuous Input model combines continuous event features with categorical asset metadata, a Mixture-of-Market-States return head, Gap, volatility-regime, and Ordinal auxiliary objectives, and full-sequence supervision. Models and preprocessing are fit using pre-2024 Train data; models are selected on 2024H2 Validation and evaluated without refitting on two 2025 Test periods. Across three independent training seeds, every model outperforms fixed single-bar LightGBM baseline in both Test halves. For the canonical checkpoint, paired gains over LightGBM are 0.029 and 0.043 bits per event. Validation experiments show that continuous input improves over discrete-token input under the same categorical return objective, full-sequence supervision improves over last-position training, and auxiliary representation shaping together with a mixture-structured return head improves return likelihood in controlled comparisons. A supporting capacity study finds that the smallest evaluated complete architecture rung achieves the strongest Validation likelihood on the present corpus.

AI.tldr: Decoder-only Transformer (VAIOM) models probabilistic next-return for one-hour FX bars using continuous input features and a categorical return head, outperforming LightGBM baselines with gains of 0.029 and 0.043 bits per event; smaller architectures can yield stronger likelihood; benefits observed for continuous inputs, full-sequence supervision, and auxiliary losses across seeds and test periods.
AI.motivation: Financial observations are continuous, heterogeneous, and noisy, but typical decoder-only models operate on discrete inputs. There is a need to preserve numerical structure at input and provide likelihood-calibrated, probabilistic next-return modeling using a unified decoder-only framework.
AI.method: Propose Vector-Input Autoregressive Inference for Ordinal-Return Modeling (VAIOM): a decoder-only Transformer that takes continuous multivariate financial-event vectors as input while predicting a categorical bucket for the next volatility-normalized return. The model uses a Mixture-of-Market-States return head, multiple auxiliary objectives (Gap, volatility-regime, Ordinal), and full-sequence supervision. A 0.9M-parameter Hybrid Continuous Input variant combines continuous features with asset metadata. Training uses pre-2024 data, validation on 2024H2, and evaluation on two 2025 test periods across three seeds; performance is compared against a fixed LightGBM baseline.
AI.result: All models outperform the LightGBM baseline in both test halves. Canonical checkpoint yields gains of 0.029 and 0.043 bits per event. Validation shows that continuous inputs improve over discrete-token inputs under the same categorical objective, full-sequence supervision improves over last-position training, and the combination of auxiliary representation shaping with a mixture-structured return head enhances return likelihood. A capacity study indicates the smallest complete architecture rung provides the strongest validation likelihood on the current corpus.
AI.conclusion: The VAIOM framework demonstrates that preserving input numerical structure via continuous inputs, coupled with a mixture-structured return head and auxiliary objectives, yields superior probabilistic next-return modeling in finance compared with a strong discrete-input baseline. The finding that smaller, complete architectures can outperform larger configurations highlights efficient design for likelihood optimization in financial time-series forecasting.

title: The 2nd International StepUP Competition for Biometric Footstep Recognition: From Steps to Strides
comment: Accepted to the 2026 IEEE International Joint Conference on Biometrics (IJCB)
summary: The International StepUP Competition Series was launched to advance research in pressure-based footstep biometrics through a standardized and challenging evaluation framework. Using the large-scale StepUP-P150 dataset (with more than 200,000 high-resolution dynamic footsteps from 150 individuals) and a previously unreleased test set, the 2nd edition of the competition addressed three key challenges: (1) generalization to unseen users with limited enrollment data, (2) robustness to domain shift caused by variations in footwear and walking speed and (3) effective fusion of paired left-right footsteps. While the first two challenges built on the inaugural competition, this edition introduced more extreme cross-domain conditions and moved beyond isolated footsteps to stride-level verification, enabling new opportunities for representation learning and inter-step information fusion. The competition attracted 26 registrants from academia and industry, with a best equal error rate of 8.00% achieved by the ArogyaPandit Research Team using a spatiotemporal CNN combined with an ensemble-based scoring strategy. The top solutions showcase the value of harnessing temporal patterns and of incorporating inference-time normalization and calibration strategies to improve scoring. However, the results also reveal that recognizing users in unseen personal footwear remains a challenge, especially in the presence of distractors with similar characteristics.

AI.tldr: A two-edition StepUP competition on pressure-based footstep biometrics used a large-scale StepUP-P150 dataset to tackle generalization to unseen users, domain shifts (footwear and speed), and left-right footstep fusion at stride level. The best system achieved 8.0% equal error rate (EER) using a spatiotemporal CNN with ensemble scoring. Results show temporal patterns and calibration help, but generalization to unseen footwear in the presence of distractors remains challenging.
AI.motivation: Advance research in pressure-based footstep biometrics through a standardized, challenging evaluation framework that assesses generalization, domain robustness, and effective fusion of paired footsteps, enabling progress in representation learning and practical verification.
AI.method: Utilized the large StepUP-P150 dataset (>200k dynamic footsteps from 150 individuals) and a novel test set in the competition. Addressed three challenges: (1) generalization to unseen users with limited enrollment data, (2) robustness to domain shifts from footwear and walking speed, (3) fusion of paired left-right footsteps at stride level. Employed a spatiotemporal CNN with ensemble-based scoring, and leveraged inference-time normalization/calibration for scoring. The setup emphasizes cross-domain conditions and stride-level verification rather than isolated footsteps.
AI.result: Best equal error rate (EER) of 8.00% achieved by the ArogyaPandit Research Team. 26 registrants participated. Top solutions highlighted the value of temporal pattern modeling and inference-time normalization/calibration. Despite progress, recognizing users with unseen footwear remains difficult, particularly with distractors of similar characteristics.
AI.conclusion: The competition demonstrates the potential of representation learning and inter-step information fusion for pressure-based footstep biometrics under challenging cross-domain conditions. However, substantial generalization gaps persist for unseen footwear, indicating the need for more extreme cross-domain scenarios and robust calibration strategies in future work.

title: TRACE: Turn-level Reward Assignment via Credit Estimation for Long-Horizon Agents
summary: Multi-turn agents solve complex tasks through extended sequences of tool interactions before producing a final answer, making credit assignment a fundamental challenge during post-training. Outcome rewards provide reliable supervision for short-horizon reasoning, but become sparse and high-variance as trajectories grow to tens or hundreds of tool calls. They can also be misleading: a failed rollout may contain many useful actions that move the agent closer to the goal, yet outcome-only training assigns them the same negative advantage as the eventual mistake. We propose TRACE (Turn-level Reward Assignment via Credit Estimation), a dense credit-assignment method for agentic reinforcement learning. TRACE represents rollouts as state transitions at tool-call boundaries, obtains gold-answer log-probabilities from a frozen reference model, transforms them into log-ratio state values, and derives per-action rewards as Temporal-Difference changes in those values. This requires no additional critic or process-label training, and its one-step log-ratio TD component telescopes across redundant tool calls. On long-horizon complex search, TRACE substantially improves base-model tool-use ability using pure RL, without a cold-start supervised fine-tuning stage, an agentic mid-training stage, or training on live-web data. On the closed-web BrowseComp-Plus benchmark, it raises Qwen3-4B from $7.2$ to $35.6$ and Qwen3-30B-A3B from $8.4$ to $42.6$. The learned search behavior also transfers to open-web benchmarks, and the learning curves show earlier improvement and faster convergence during RL training.

AI.tldr: TRACE is a dense credit-assignment method for agentic reinforcement learning that uses log-ratio state values derived from a frozen reference model's gold-answer probabilities to assign per-action rewards at tool-call boundaries, enabling effective long-horizon tool use via one-step TD updates without extra critics or live-data training.
AI.motivation: Credit assignment in multi-turn tool-use tasks is challenging due to sparse, high-variance, and potentially misleading outcome rewards as trajectories grow long.
AI.method: Represent rollouts as state transitions at tool-call boundaries; obtain gold-answer log-probabilities from a frozen reference model; convert to log-ratio state values; derive per-action rewards as Temporal-Difference changes in those values; no additional critic or process-label training; one-step log-ratio TD telescopes across redundant tool calls.
AI.result: In long-horizon search, TRACE yields substantial improvements in base-model tool-use via pure RL without extra fine-tuning. On the BrowseComp-Plus benchmark, Qwen3-4B improves from 7.2 to 35.6 and Qwen3-30B-A3B from 8.4 to 42.6; learned search behavior generalizes to open-web benchmarks with faster convergence.
AI.conclusion: TRACE provides dense, efficient credit assignment for agentic RL without extra supervision stages, improving tool-use performance and enabling transfer across benchmarks.

title: Thresholded Cross-Attention for Reliable Intensity-Chromaticity Fusion in Low-Light Image Enhancement
summary: Low-Light Image Enhancement (LLIE) requires a careful balance among noise suppression, color fidelity, and efficiency. Recent HVI-based methods alleviate color entanglement by decoupling intensity and chromaticity, yet how reliably the two streams are fused again is an overlooked factor that largely determines the final quality. We observe that the confidence of cross-stream attention is strongly layer-dependent, so the fixed-quota selection of Top-K sparse attention is mismatched to it, discarding informative dependencies in some layers while retaining noisy ones in others. Motivated by this observation, we propose TCA-Net, a network built around Thresholded Cross-Attention that targets reliable intensity-chromaticity fusion in the HVI space rather than introducing yet another color representation. At its core, TCA replaces the rigid Top-K quota with a fixed confidence threshold whose retained cardinality is input- and layer-adaptive, retaining only high-confidence cross-stream interactions while suppressing unreliable ones. Around this core, two complementary designs clean up the fusion before and after it: a Phase-guided Fourier Interaction Module provides a structure-aware brightness initialization for the intensity stream prior to fusion, and a Decoupled Dual-Stream Guidance Module constructs residual intensity features to suppress chromaticity leakage during reconstruction. A Scale-Aware Consistency Regularization further improves structural robustness under scale perturbations during training. Extensive experiments on LOL-v1, LOL-v2, Sony-Total-Dark, and LSRW-Huawei demonstrate that TCA-Net delivers competitive restoration accuracy, improved color fidelity, and a compact parameter size.

AI.tldr: Adaptive thresholded cross-attention (TCA) for robust intensity–chromaticity fusion in HVI space, replacing fixed Top-K with a confidence-threshold, aided by Phase-guided Fourier Init, Decoupled Dual-Stream Guidance, and Scale-Aware regularization; achieves competitive LLIE performance with better color fidelity and efficiency.
AI.motivation: LLIE methods using high-level vision infrared (HVI) decouple intensity and chromaticity but rely on cross-stream fusion. Fixed Top-K attention is not sensitive to layer-wise confidence, causing information loss or noise. The work seeks a reliable, adaptive fusion mechanism to improve color fidelity while maintaining efficiency.
AI.method: Introduce TCA-Net with Thresholded Cross-Attention that uses a confidence threshold to select cross-stream interactions, adaptively varying with input and layer. Complementary modules: Phase-guided Fourier Interaction Module for structure-aware brightness initialization; Decoupled Dual-Stream Guidance Module to generate residual intensity features and curb chromatic leakage; Scale-Aware Consistency Regularization during training to improve robustness to scale perturbations.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation on LOL-v1, LOL-v2, Sony-Total-Dark, and LSRW-Huawei shows TCA-Net achieves competitive restoration accuracy, improved color fidelity, and a compact parameter count compared to baselines.
AI.conclusion: Adaptive, threshold-based cross-attention with supportive fusion modules effectively couples intensity and chromaticity in HVI space, yielding robust LLIE performance with improved color fidelity and efficiency across multiple datasets.

title: Lyapunov Exponent as Physics-Informed Dense Reward: RL Discovery of Stabilization Beyond the Kapitza Pendulum
summary: We suggest using the Lyapunov characteristic exponent (LCE) as a dense reward signal for the reinforcement learning problem of stabilizing the inverted pendulum with vertical motion. With LCE, the agent not only successfully found the oscillatory motion known as the Kapitza pendulum but also damped the pendulum's pivoting, leaving it in a strictly upright position.

AI.tldr: Proposes Lyapunov characteristic exponent (LCE) as a dense reward for RL in stabilizing an inverted pendulum with vertical motion; results in Kapitza pendulum dynamics and upright stabilization.
AI.motivation: Address reward design for RL in unstable, nonlinear, time-varying systems by using a continuous stability metric (LCE) to guide learning toward robust upright stabilization and damping of pivot motion.
AI.method: Compute the LCE along trajectories and use it as a dense reward signal in RL for the inverted pendulum with vertical pivot motion, aiming to induce stability (negative LCE) and realizable Kapitza pendulum behavior.
AI.result: The agent not only learns the oscillatory Kapitza pendulum motion but also damped pivoting, achieving a strictly upright posture.
AI.conclusion: LCE-based dense rewards can effectively guide RL in complex nonlinear dynamics, enabling concurrent discovery of oscillatory and stabilized regimes; Lyapunov-structured signals show promise for stabilizing controllers in non-linear systems.

title: Cyclone: Diffusion Model for Cycle-Consistent Weather Editing from Unpaired Driving Data
summary: Reliable perception under diverse weather conditions remains a major challenge for autonomous driving systems. A common strategy to improve robustness is either to synthesize adverse weather conditions for training perception models or to apply weather-removal techniques to recover clean inputs. However, existing approaches typically rely on synthetic data augmentation or physics-based, task-specific models that require paired training data and often struggle to generate realistic weather effects or generalize robustly to out-of-domain scenarios. Toward this problem, we present Cyclone, a unified framework for weather editing based on latent diffusion, equipped with cycle-consistent constraints and knowledge from image-text models. Cyclone enables the generation of multiple weather conditions across diverse scenes while eliminating the need for paired data. Experimental results show that our approach produces more realistic, structure-preserving outputs than existing baselines and leads to consistent improvements across several downstream driving perception tasks.
